Resource card: ends with a date and outlink icon, a download link, or a text-link CTA with optional copy.

Usage notes

The Resource card from the Figma Cards page: an image, the resource type and a title, ending in one of three approved actions.

Provide: title, resourceType, href and an action; optionally image and flag.

action Footer Also pass
link (default) The date on the left, a qualys-blue outlink icon on the right date ("Dec 10, 2026")
download A blue download text link with the download icon before it cta ("Get the Report")
cta The neutral text link with an arrow cta ("Learn More"), and optionally description
  • Shell: White, radius-lg, shadow-card, 16px padding, at least 400px tall, so footers line up across a row. With href the whole card is the link: on hover a 6px qualys-blue bar slides in along the bottom edge and the outlink icon nudges up and to the right.
  • Image: 318 × 174 in a 350px card (about 16:9), radius-media (8px) corners; flag puts a Flag on its top left corner. The Figma CTA variant has no flag.
  • Resource type: IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-secondary, 16px above the title (not blue, unlike the event and webinar type).
  • Title: SemiBold 20px, line height 1.3, −1%.
  • Description (CTA action only): Regular 16px text-secondary, 16px under the title.
  • Approved button types: outlink icon, download CTA, text link (tertiary). No primary button.

WebinarCard

Component

Webinar card, default and featured. Every number of speakers, from none to more than six.

Usage notes

The Webinar card from the Figma Cards page: an image, "Webinar | format | duration", a title, the speaker and the date.

Provide: title, format, duration, date, href; optionally image, flag, speakers ({ name, company, image }) and, for the featured layout, a description. category defaults to "Webinar".

  • Shell: White, radius-lg, shadow-card, 16px padding, at least 400px tall, so footers line up across a row. With href the whole card is the link: on hover a 6px qualys-blue bar slides in along the bottom edge and the outlink icon nudges up and to the right.
  • Image: 16:9, radius-media (8px) corners; flag puts a Flag on its top left corner (flagTone picks the tier). Without an image the ecru ground shows.
  • Meta row: "Webinar" in Medium 16px text-accent-primary, then the format and the duration in IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-secondary, separated by a rhino "|". The duration has a 14px qualys-blue clock (time icon).
  • Title: SemiBold 20px, line height 1.3, −1%.
  • Speaker: 40px avatar (photo or the avatar-bg placeholder), 8px, name in SemiBold 16px (two lines at most).
  • The speaker rule. Speakers sit on one row that never wraps, so cards in a row keep the same height. Named speakers come first; the rest stack as headshots overlapping by 15px, three circles at most. When more people are unnamed than fit, the third circle shows "+N", where N counts every speaker who isn't named.
Speakers Default card Featured card
None No speaker row No speaker row
1 Avatar and name Avatar, name and company
2 First named, 1 headshot Both named, with company
3 First named, 2 headshots Two named, 1 headshot
4 First named, 3 headshots Two named, 2 headshots
5 First named, 2 headshots and "+4" Two named, 3 headshots
6 First named, 2 headshots and "+5" Two named, 2 headshots and "+4"
More than 6 First named, 2 headshots and "+N" Two named, 2 headshots and "+N"
- Footer: the date in Medium 16px text-secondary ("Tue Dec 10, 2026") and the outlink icon.
- Approved button type: the outlink icon, the same as the other content cards. Figma's usage note also lists a primary button; it is not used on this card (review decision).
- Featured (layout="featured"): one card across the full width, 320px tall, image on the left (47%, radius-md), copy on the right. It applies from 1024px; on tablet and mobile the card stacks like the default. It names the first two speakers with their company (Regular 16px text-secondary), then the description; see the speaker rule. Once it has stacked, the speaker row may wrap.
- Figma's default webinar card has no bar track (409px); this one keeps the track every card has, so it runs 6px taller.
- The speaker rule was set in review: Figma draws one speaker on the default card and gives no layout for more. "+N" means the same here as on DrawerCard.

EventCard

Component

Event card: default (in a grid) and featured (full width from 1024px). Hover for the blue bar.

Usage notes

The Event card from the Figma Cards page: an image, the event type and format, a title and the date, ending in an outlink icon.

Provide: title, category (the event type), format, date, href; optionally image, flag, and for the featured layout a description.

  • Shell: White, radius-lg, shadow-card, 16px padding, at least 400px tall, so footers line up across a row. With href the whole card is the link: on hover a 6px qualys-blue bar slides in along the bottom edge and the outlink icon nudges up and to the right.
  • Image: 16:9, radius-media (8px) corners; flag puts a Flag on its top left corner (flagTone picks the tier). Without an image the ecru ground shows.
  • Meta row: event type in Wix Madefor Text Medium 16px text-accent-primary, a rhino "|", then the format in IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-secondary. 16px above the title.
  • Title: SemiBold 20px, line height 1.3, −1%.
  • Footer, pinned to the bottom: the date in Medium 16px text-secondary on the left, a 20px qualys-blue outlink icon on the right.
  • Date: short date, a bullet, then the time: "Dec 10, 2026 • 11a PST".
  • Approved button type: the outlink icon only. No text link or button.
  • Featured (layout="featured"): one card across the full width, 320px tall, image on the left (47%, radius-md), copy on the right. It applies from 1024px; on tablet and mobile the card stacks like the default. The description (Regular 16px text-secondary) shows only here.

IntegrationCard

Component

Integration card with a thumbnail and name, or a logo. Extra

Usage notes

The Integration card from the Figma Cards page: a partner integration with its thumbnail and name (or its logo) above a short list of labelled facts.

Provide: name, and either image (a square thumbnail) or logo (a wide logo, which replaces the thumbnail and name). Then type, worksWith (a list), dataFetched and category; href makes the card a link. maxTags sets how many "works with" tags show (default 2); labels renames the four labels.

  • Shell: White, radius-lg, shadow-card, 16px padding. With href the whole card is the link: on hover a 6px qualys-blue bar slides in along the bottom edge and the arrow nudges forward; the shadow does not change. 260px wide in the Figma frames.
  • Top: 56px thumbnail with radius-md (the avatar-bg tile shows until an image loads), 16px, then the name in SemiBold 18px. The logo variant shows the logo at 37px tall instead.
  • Rule: 1px stroke-neutral-400, 16px above and below.
  • Facts: label in SemiBold 12px uppercase, +5%, text-secondary; 4px; value in IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-primary. 20px between facts, in this order: Type, Works With, Data Fetched, Category.
  • Works With: small outline badges, 8px apart; tags past maxTags fold into a "+N" badge.
  • Figma's usage note for this card repeats the Standard card's; the layout rules there (stack on mobile, load more past eight) apply here too.

InlinePromoCard

Component

Inline promo: vertical on the blue gradient or Charcoal, wide, and banner. Wide and banner stack on mobile.

Usage notes

The Inline Promo card from the Figma Cards page: a promotion on Charcoal or the blue gradient with a white heading, one line of copy and one call to action, in a vertical, wide or banner layout.

Provide: title, description, cta (the label) and href. Choose color (light is the blue gradient, dark is Charcoal) and layout. Optional: logo (the reversed Qualys logo URL), image (a product image), icon (general-events, general-webinar or general-resource) and button (primary or tertiary).

Figma name Props Size in Figma Approved button
Inline Promo, Product layout="vertical", logo, image 331 × 510 Primary
Inline Promo Wide, Product layout="horizontal", logo, image 752 × 269 Primary
Inline Promo Banner, Product layout="banner", image 752 × 184 Tertiary
Inline Promo / Resource Hub Center with Icon color="dark", logo, icon 331 × 400, three in a row Primary
  • Surface: radius-lg, shadow-drawer. light is blue-gradient-start to blue-gradient-end; dark is surface-neutral-600.
  • Heading: h2 (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 38px, line height 1.1, −2%), text-inverted. Copy: IBM Plex Sans Regular 16px, text-inverted, 16px under the heading.
  • Logo: the reversed logo (red shield, white wordmark) at 37px tall, top left. Icon: a general icon, 43px tall, in icon-inverted, 16px above the heading.
  • CTA: primary is a small Qualys Red button; tertiary is the inverted text link with an arrow. The whole card is the link.
  • Vertical: 16px padding; the image sits between the logo and the heading. With a logo or icon and no image the card is at least 400px tall and the button sits at the bottom.
  • Wide and banner: 24px padding (spacing-xl); copy on the left 60%, the image bleeding off the right edge. The banner has no logo.
  • Mobile (under 768px): wide and banner stack like the vertical card, image above the heading. On tablet the vertical card just grows wider.
  • Red on the blue gradient is the Figma pairing for these cards; don't swap in other button colours.

TestimonialCard

Component

A customer quote card: large, large on a photo, small, and with a video. The logos here are placeholders.

Usage notes

A customer quote from the Figma Testimonials page: the customer's logo, the quote, who said it and a link to the story.

Provide: quote, name, company, logo and logoAlt; optionally avatar, link, size, image or video.

Figma name Props What it shows
Large Testimonial Card default 939 × 500px, the quote in quote-lg (32px)
Full Image Background Large Testimonial Card image The same over a photo, with the quote on a white panel
Small Testimonial Card size="sm" 500px wide, the quote in quote-md (24px)
Video Testimonial Card video The small card with a portrait clip on the right
  • White, radius-lg, shadow-drawer. Padding is 36px (large) or 24px (small).
  • Logo: up to 60px tall, at the top left; 24px below it, the quote.
  • Foot, pinned to the bottom: a 40px Avatar with the name (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 16px) over the company (text-secondary), and on the right a neutral TextLink with the arrow, "Read the Story".
  • On a photo: the picture fills the card with a hairline edge; the content sits on a panel 62% wide, white at 90%, radius-md, 24px padding.
  • With a video: the clip is 312px wide with radius-rg, 24px from the copy, with the play button. The person shows without an avatar. With no video, leave video out and the quote takes the full width.
  • Mobile (inside TestimonialCarousel): 300px wide, 16px padding, a hairline edge; the quote drops to 16px; the link moves under the person. A video moves to the top at 16:9.

Video behaviour, from the Figma usage notes:

  • Use one aspect ratio for every clip, preferably 9:16, with a clear, uncluttered thumbnail.
  • On hover the thumbnail may play silently; pressing play opens the video in a modal that dims the page, with the usual controls and a close button. Handle that with video={{ video: true, poster, onPlay }}.
  • Video cards and small cards can share one carousel.

Do / Don't:

  • Do keep quotes under about 200 characters, in the customer's words, inside quotation marks.
  • Do give the logo logoAlt text (the company name).
  • Don't use a busy photo behind the panel.

Notes:

  • The large card is drawn with a different shadow (0 4px 24px at 10%) from the others; all use shadow-drawer.
  • The Figma usage notes for the non-video cards are still placeholders.

StatCard

Component

One figure with its label: large and medium, filled and outlined.

Usage notes

One figure from the Figma Stats page: a feature icon, a large number with its unit, a short label and one line of description.

Provide: value and label; optionally suffix ("%", "x") or prefix ("#"), icon (a Feature Icon), description, tone and size.

  • Tone: solid (default) is qualys-blue with white figures and a misty-blue description; outline is a 1px qualys-blue outline with blue figures and a text-secondary description.
  • Large (lg, three in a row): 36px padding. The number is stat-lg (Bold 86px) with its unit at 48px on the same baseline; the label is Wix Madefor Text Medium 38px; the description is paragraph-rg, 16px below.
  • Medium (md, four in a row): 16px top and 24px side and bottom padding. Number stat-md (64px) with a 38px unit; label Medium 24px.
  • Icon: a Feature Icon in a 56px box, 8px above the number.
  • radius-lg. Cards in a row share the tallest height.
  • Count up: the number runs from 0 to its value once, when the card first scrolls into view: 1.2 seconds, easing out. The unit and label don't move. People who prefer reduced motion see the final number straight away, and so does a value that isn't one plain number ("24/7"). Screen readers get the final value only. countUp={false} turns it off.
  • Mobile (inside Stats): 24px padding; the number and its unit are both 48px (38px and 36px in medium); the label is 24px (20px in medium).

Use Stats to lay out three or four of these with the right gaps and mobile sizes.

Content, from the Figma usage notes:

  • Lead with the metric, then an action verb and the value: "150% Faster Detection". Keep the label and description under 120 characters together.
  • Three in a row suits impact figures: reductions, time saved, efficiency gains. Four in a row suits mixed figures: counts, capabilities, rankings.

Watch out:

  • White on qualys-blue is 3.8:1, which is enough for the large number and label but not for small text. Keep the description short and never put anything essential only there.

Components

Avatars and profiles

Avatar

Component

Small and medium are circles, large is a square. Each shows the default silhouette until a photo is set.

Usage notes

The avatar from the Figma Avatars page: a person's photo, or the default silhouette when there is none.

Provide: image and size (sm, md or lg); add alt with the person's name only when the avatar stands alone. Beside a written name, leave alt out so the name isn't read twice.

Size Shape Use it for
Small, 40px Circle Event, standard and testimonial cards, compact lists, tables, drawers and accordions
Medium, 56px Circle Figma leaves this usage blank; use it where 40px reads too small, such as an author line
Large, 300px Square, radius-md Featured speakers and profile cards
  • Shape follows size: circles are for small, inline avatars; the square is for large, profile contexts (over 56px). Never mix shapes at the same size. The default avatar takes the same shape.
  • Default avatar: an avatar-bg ground with the avatar-icon silhouette (15px, 24px and 80px wide). It shows when no photo was uploaded, the data is missing or anonymised, the image fails to load, or it was removed. Never show a broken-image icon, and always keep the space reserved.
  • Cropping: square photos keep the face at 60 to 70% of the frame (never over 80% or under 50%). Circular photos keep the face centred with no features cut off.
  • Backgrounds: clean, simple and professional. Solid colours, subtle gradients, a soft-focus office or a neutral indoor setting are fine. Avoid busy patterns, high contrast, distracting elements, uneven lighting and heavy shadows.
  • Use avatars for authors, review and testimonial quotes, user, team and member lists, and speaker profiles and bios: wherever a person speaks, acts or contributes.
  • Don't use avatars as decoration, mix crops or shapes in one list, use random colours for the default, or leave a blank space where a photo is missing. Keep the spacing between avatars equal.
  • Profile text beside an avatar, the same everywhere (cards, drawers, hover cards, profile cards and the modal): the name in title-sm (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 16px, line height 1.3, text-primary); 4px; the role in paragraph-rg (IBM Plex Sans Regular 16px, text-secondary); the company in the same style at Medium (500), or as its logo. Never set a person's name larger than 16px.
  • Avatars that link to nothing keep the default cursor and have no hover state.
  • Figma's usage note lists an Extra Large (320px) size for keynote speakers, but none is drawn and an earlier review ruled out extra-large avatars, so there is no xl. The note also gives #D9CFC1 and #888888 for the default avatar; the drawn avatars use avatar-bg (#E6DDCB) and avatar-icon (#A6A094), which is what this uses.

ProfileCard

Component

Hover or focus the first two cards to see Read Bio (nothing opens here). The third is not interactive.

Usage notes

The profile card from the Figma Avatars page: a large square photo with a profile-link chip, the name, the designation and the company logo. With a bio, hovering shows "Read Bio" and a click opens the ProfileModal.

Provide: name; optionally designation, image, logo, link ({ href, network }) and onOpen. For a row of people, use ProfileGrid, which wires up the modal for you.

  • Card: surface-neutral-300 (Ecru), radius-lg, no shadow. Padding 24px on desktop, 16px on tablet and mobile.
  • Photo: full card width, 300px tall (303 × 287 on mobile), radius-md. Without a photo, or if it fails to load, the default avatar shows (see Avatar for cropping and background rules).
  • Chip: a SocialButton (52px, radius-rg, icon-bg-default) 16px in from the photo's top right corner; it opens the person's profile in a new tab. It shows the LinkedIn glyph by default; link.network switches it to x, facebook, instagram or url. Screen readers hear "Jonathan Doe on LinkedIn".
  • Text: 16px under the photo, the profile text used everywhere: the name in title-sm (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 16px, line height 1.3), the role in paragraph-rg text-secondary, 4px under it (see Avatar); 20px; the logo at 40px tall.
  • Interactive (onOpen set): hover or keyboard focus covers the photo with charcoal at 85% and an outlined white "Read Bio" button; clicking anywhere on the card calls onOpen. The chip stays a separate link. Change the wording with bioLabel.
  • Not interactive (no onOpen): default cursor, no hover effect.
  • bare drops the card ground and padding; ProfileGrid uses it for the combined container.
  • Figma's "Read Bio" button measures about 111 × 54px; this uses the system's large inverted secondary Button (50px tall).

ProfileModal

Component

The bio panel, shown in place here. On a page it opens over a 70% black backdrop; use ProfileGrid to try it.

Usage notes

The bio modal from the Figma Avatars page. It opens when a profile card is clicked: the photo, name, designation and logo on the left, an "About" text on the right.

Provide: open, onClose, name and the bio as children (a string or paragraphs); optionally designation, image, logo, link and links ({ network, href }). ProfileGrid does this for you.

  • Backdrop: the dark overlay (overlay-dark, black at 50%). Clicking it closes the modal.
  • Panel: white, radius-lg, shadow-drawer, 24px padding, up to 1128px wide and centred; the height follows the bio up to 80% of the viewport, then the panel scrolls.
  • Left: 320px square photo (radius-md) with the same 52px chip as the card; the profile text used everywhere: name title-sm (SemiBold 16px), designation paragraph-rg text-secondary (see Avatar), and the logo at 40px.
  • Right: 56px from the photo. "About" in SemiBold 16px uppercase, +5%, text-secondary; 24px; the bio in IBM Plex Sans Regular 18px, line height 1.3, −1%.
  • Close: a cross top right with a 44px hit area. Esc and the backdrop close it too.
  • Motion: fades and rises in over 300ms; no motion with reduced-motion settings.
  • Tablet: 300px photo, 36px gap. Mobile: a bottom sheet up to 95% of the viewport height, 16px padding, photo on top; the name stays at 16px and the bio is 16px.
  • Accessibility: role="dialog" named by the person's name; focus moves to the close button, stays inside the modal, and returns to the card on close. The page behind doesn't scroll while it is open.
  • links adds a row of social links bottom right: plain SocialButtons (16px glyphs in text-secondary, 16px apart) in the order LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, URL. A link with no network or icon shows as a text label.
  • inline shows the panel in the page flow with no backdrop or close button, as in Figma's second drawing.
  • Figma's usage note says "max-width 600px"; every drawn modal is 1128px wide (809px on tablet), so this follows the drawings.

ProfileGrid

Pattern

Individual cards and the combined container. Click a card to open its bio; Esc closes it.

Usage notes

The profile layouts from the Figma Avatars page: a row of profile cards that open a bio modal.

Provide: items ({ name, designation, image, logo, link, bio, links }) and layout. A person with a bio gets the "Read Bio" hover and opens a ProfileModal; a person without one is not interactive.

Layout Desktop (1024px and up) Tablet (768px and up) Mobile
individual (default) 3 cards across, 24px gaps 2 across, 16px gaps 1 across, 16px gaps
combined One Ecru container, 5 people across, 24px padding and gaps 3 across, 16px Stacked, 16px
  • Individual: each person is a ProfileCard. In the 1200px container the cards are 384 × 464px.
  • Combined: one surface-neutral-300 container with radius-lg; the photos are square (about 211px on desktop) and keep the LinkedIn chip, name, designation and logo. Up to five people in a row.
  • Put the grid inside .q-container so it follows the page margins. Extra people wrap onto the next row.
  • bioLabel, aboutLabel and closeLabel change the wording of "Read Bio", "About" and the close button.

Components

Tags and flags

Tag

Component

Badges in nine tones, three fills and two sizes; text, label and eyebrow tags; vulnerability metadata

Usage notes

Badges and text tags from the Figma Tagging System: a badge signals status (recency, availability, urgency); a text tag names a category.

Provide: one or two words as children. Badge: variant (fill, light or outline), tone, size. Text tag: variant="text", and href when it links.

Figma type Use Interactive
Badge (fill / light / outline) Status: "New" on a mega-menu product heading, content type on a card image, severity No
Text tag (text) Categories: blog topics, labels in lists, "New" in the nav menu Sometimes (href)
FilterChip Filtering a list Always
Flag Notices anchored to a container edge No
Marker Unread or active item in a tab or menu No
  • Badge: 26px tall (rg, tag-sm 14px) or 25px (sm, tag-xs 12px); 8px side padding inside a 1.5px stroke; radius-sm (6px); Wix Madefor Text Bold, uppercase, +5% / +3% tracking.
  • Fill: white text on the tone. Light: the tone at 15% with tone-coloured text (gray uses ash with asphalt; slate uses tag-slate-tint with asphalt). Outline: 1.5px tone stroke and tone text (gray uses a rhino stroke).
  • Tones: purple tag-purple, blue qualys-blue, dark-red pepper, red tag-red (light fill uses qualys-red), green tag-green, orange tag-orange, yellow tag-yellow, gray asphalt, slate tag-slate. Each tone has a fixed meaning in vulnerability metadata (below); always keep the word, never let the colour stand alone.
  • Text tag: tag-md (18px, 16px on mobile) Medium in text-accent-primary, no fill; as a link it turns Cobalt on hover.
  • Label tag (variant="label"): label at Regular weight, 16px IBM Plex Sans in text-primary. A plain descriptor beside a value or an icon.
  • Eyebrow tag (variant="eyebrow"): eyebrow-xs, 12px SemiBold capitals with +5% letter spacing in text-primary. A small overline on a card or tile. Both take href to become links.
  • Contrast (as designed, flagged): yellow (1.7:1), orange (2.8:1), green (3.3:1) and blue (3.8:1) badges fall below 4.5:1 for 12–14px text, in every variant; the red light fill is 3.8:1. Purple, dark red, red fill, gray and slate pass. The blue text tag is 3.8:1 at 18px Medium.
  • Wording: tags label, they never ask. A tag names a status, a category or a fact: "New", "Beta", "100+ Connectors", "Critical". No action words or calls to action ("Discover", "Learn", "Try", "Get", "See", "Register", "Download", "Join"). If the reader should do something, use a TextLink or Button beside the tag instead. One to three words, no full stops.
  • Which size: rg on cards and in content; sm in tables, filters, the nav menus and next to 14–16px text. sm is the smallest; don't scale a badge down further.
  • The doc's table calls badges "pill-shaped", but every badge component uses radius-sm; this follows the components.

Vulnerability metadata (from the Chips & Badges Showcase). Each set uses badges (rg, uppercase); the tone carries the same meaning everywhere, and the word is always shown.

Set What it shows Badges
Severity Classification by CVSS score Critical: fill dark-red · High: fill red · Medium: fill orange · Low: fill yellow · Informational: fill purple
Status Where remediation stands Open: fill orange · In Progress: fill yellow · Fixed: fill green · Accepted Risk: fill gray
Impact Whether live environments are affected Affected: light red · Not Affected: light green
Exploitability Public exploit code, or a confirmed weaponised exploit Exploitable: fill red · Known Exploit: fill orange · No Known Exploit: fill green
Disclosure How public the vulnerability details are Publicly Disclosed (PUB): outline orange · Privately Disclosed (PVT): outline blue
  • Show one badge per set for an item, in this order: severity, status, impact, exploitability, disclosure.
  • Keep the labels as written (Title Case in the source, drawn in capitals by the badge). Abbreviations (PUB, PVT) follow the full words.
  • White text on the yellow Low and In Progress badges is 1.7:1 and on orange 2.8:1, under 4.5:1; kept as in the showcase and flagged for the accessibility review.

Flag

Component

The three flag tiers in two sizes. Anchor one to the top left corner of a card or image.

Usage notes

The flag-style tag from the Figma Tagging System: a high-priority notice or promotion anchored to a container edge — "Upcoming", "New" or "Featured".

Provide: a word or two as children and a tone. Position it yourself, flush with the top left corner of the card or image (position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0).

  • Shape: top-left and bottom-right corners radius-rg (10px), the other two square, so it sits in a corner.
  • Size: large (the default) is 32px tall, 12px side padding, tag-rg 16px Medium; small (size="sm") is 26px tall, 12px side padding, tag-sm 14px SemiBold, for small cards and tiles. Both have white text on flag-tier-1 (purple), flag-tier-2 (orange) or flag-tier-3 (teal).
  • Figma doesn't say which tier means what; keep the meaning consistent across a page.
  • White on tier 2 (3.54:1) and tier 3 (3.34:1) is under 4.5:1 — kept as designed, flagged. Tier 1 passes.

Marker

Component

Edge bar for unread or active items, on a left or right edge; opens into a count

Usage notes

The marker from the Figma Tagging System: a vertical bar on the edge of a tab or menu item that marks it unread or active; it can open into a pill with a count.

Provide: tone (1, 2, 3 or "blue"); count to show the open pill; label with the meaning in words ("88 unread") when it isn't said elsewhere.

  • Closed: 6 × 36px bar in marker-1, marker-2 or marker-3. These are the flag colours: each marker token points at flag-tier-1, -2 or -3, so a marker and a flag of the same number always match. The left edge is flat and the two right corners are rounded radius-xs (4px), so it sits flush against the left edge of the item.
  • Blue (tone="blue", marker-blue, which is qualys-blue): for the active item where the three flag tiers don't apply, such as the open row in AccordionModule's list, where it slides from row to row. Added in review; Figma has three tones.
  • Open: 34px tall, at least 27px wide, flat on the left with the two right corners rounded radius-media (8px); the count in white, 14px Medium, +5% tracking.
  • Side: side="left" (the default) rounds the right corners, for a left edge; side="right" rounds the left corners, for a right edge.
  • Active rows: the blue marker is how every list of tabs and menu rows shows the active one, together with a Misty Blue ground. See States and Motion.
  • Without label it is hidden from screen readers — make sure the active or unread state is also in the text or aria-current.
  • The white count is 8.1:1 on marker 1; on marker 2 (3.54:1) and marker 3 (3.34:1) it is under 4.5:1, the same as the flags, flagged. On the blue marker it is 3.78:1, also flagged. The bars themselves pass 3:1.
  • Figma draws the markers in their own darker shades (#80458A, #CB5602, #2F7F7B); they use the flag colours here, as asked in review.

EventType

Component

The five event types: icon and label

Usage notes

The event-type label from the Figma Tagging System: a 24px icon and its name, for event listings and event cards.

Provide: type — qualys, webinar, industry, speaking or training. Children override the label only if the wording must change.

type Label Icon colour
qualys Qualys Event qualys-red (the shield)
webinar Webinar event-webinar
industry Industry Event tag-slate
speaking Speaking Engagement event-speaking
training Training icon-default
  • Label Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 16px, line height 1.1, −1%, text-primary; 6px after the icon (4px for Qualys Event), as in Figma.
  • Icons are copied from the Figma components: event-* in the Icon component and the Event Icons group.
  • Use the type's own label and icon together; don't recolour the icons.

Components

Accordions and drawers

Accordion

Component

A group of drawers: standard rows or session cards. Opening one closes the others.

Usage notes

A group of drawers from the Figma Accordion page: sections that expand and collapse so a page stays compact while the detail is one click away. Two kinds: standard (ruled rows) and cards (session cards).

Provide: items and a variant. Standard items take { id, title, icon, content, cta }; card items take { id, time, title, content, speakers, cta } (the same parts as Drawer and DrawerCard). defaultOpen names the item (id or index) to start open. Opening one closes the others; pass multiple to let several stay open, or collapsible={false} to keep one open at all times (the open row can't be closed, only swapped). For an accordion as a whole page section, use AccordionModule.

Variant Use it for Looks like
standard Secondary information people read one section at a time: FAQs, legal disclaimers, technical specifications; many categories with little visual noise; nested information where cards would look bulky Drawer rows stacked with shared rules
cards Event or session lists where time and title come first; items with an action ("Register") people can take without opening; content that should feel like distinct entities DrawerCards stacked 16px apart; every Register or Join Waitlist button is the same width (see DrawerCard)
  • How many: at least 4 drawers, at most 12.
  • Default state: all collapsed; the first may start open when it holds the primary information.
  • Standard, icons: give every item an icon or none — Figma has an "Icon + Text" type and a "Text" type, not a mix.
  • Width: the accordion fills its container. In the Figma layouts that is the content width inside the page margins on mobile, tablet and desktop; session cards run up to 1144px wide, centred, on desktop and larger.
  • Mobile and tablet (under 1024px): standard rows tighten to a 48px pitch with no side padding, a 24px icon and 16px above the CTA; cards keep their 16px gap and follow DrawerCard's mobile layout under 768px. layout="mobile" passes the phone layout to every row at any screen width.
  • Each row or card keeps Drawer's and DrawerCard's own rules (headings, aria-expanded, motion, character limits).
  • The session cards drawn on the Accordion page differ slightly from the Drawers page (18px names, no speaker shown while closed). That page points to the Drawers page for the cards, so this uses DrawerCard as is.
  • Figma doesn't say whether several sections may be open at once; one at a time follows its "one section at a time" guidance.

Drawer

Component

Standard drawer: click a row to open it; with or without an icon, button or text link; desktop and mobile

Usage notes

The Standard drawer from the Figma Drawers page: a ruled row with a title that expands downward to show detail — the system's accordion row. Closed it is compact; open it reveals body copy and an optional call to action.

Provide: title, body copy as children, and optionally icon (a feature icon URL or node) and cta (a small Button or a TextLink). defaultOpen starts it open; or control it with open + onToggle. For a list of them, use Accordion.

  • Row: 56px tall closed, between two 1px stroke-neutral-400 rules (stacked drawers share a rule, so rows repeat every 56px). 16px above and below the title, 8px at the sides.
  • Title: Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 18px, line height 1.3, −1%, text-primary; Title Case. Keep it under 180 characters and two lines.
  • Icon: optional feature icon in a 32px box, 8px before the title (Feature Icons group).
  • Trigger: a 16px chevron on the right — down when closed, rotating to up when open. The whole row is the button.
  • Body: IBM Plex Sans Regular 16px, line height 1.3, text-primary; keep it under 500 characters so it doesn't run long on mobile. The CTA sits 24px below the copy; 16px closes the row.
  • Motion: the panel animates its height over 300ms and the chevron turns over 200ms; neither moves for people who prefer reduced motion.
  • Mobile and tablet (under 1024px): rows repeat every 48px, with no side padding, a 24px icon, 16px above the CTA and 12px closing the row. layout="mobile" shows this layout at any screen width (the preview uses it to show a phone screen).
  • Exposed as a heading (level 3 by default, headingLevel) holding a button with aria-expanded; the panel is a labelled region. Keyboard focus shows focus-ring.
  • For session cards with a time, speakers and a Register button, use DrawerCard.

DrawerCard

Component

Session card drawer: none to more than six profiles, with and without a button, at four widths, and on mobile.

Usage notes

The card drawer from the Figma Drawers page, built for event agendas: a white card with a time, a session title and a chevron that opens to show the description, with zero to many speaker profiles and an optional call to action.

Provide: title; optionally time (the overline), a description as children, speakers ({ name, designation, company, image }) and cta (a secondary Button such as "Register"). defaultOpen, or open + onToggle, set the state.

  • Card: white, radius-lg, shadow-drawer, 24px padding (16px on mobile). Time in IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-secondary; 10px; title in Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 24px, line height 1.1, −2% (under 180 characters, clamped at two lines). A 30px chevron sits top right, level with the time.
  • Open: the description (Regular 16px, under 500 characters) appears 10px under the title; profiles follow 20px below.
  • Profile: 40px round headshot (or the avatar-bg placeholder), 16px, then name (SemiBold 16px), designation (Regular 16px text-secondary) and company (Medium 16px text-secondary).

The profile rule. How much each profile shows depends on how many there are. A closed card always keeps its profiles on one row.

Profiles Closed: each profile shows Closed: layout With a button
None — Time and title only The button sits beside the title
1 First and last name, role, company One profile across the row Button at the right end of the row
2 Name, role, company Two equal columns Same; the columns share what is left
3 Name, role (two lines at most, then "…"), company Three equal columns Same
4 Name and company One row, each profile as wide as its text Same
5 Name and company One row Same
6 First name over surname, and company One row Four are named; the fifth and sixth stack as headshots with "+2"
More than 6 The first four: first name over surname, and company The rest stack as headshots overlapping by 15px, four circles at most The last circle shows "+N"
  • "+N" counts everyone in the stack (every profile that isn't named). It shows with a button, or when the stack holds more than four people.
  • Open (any number): everyone is listed in two columns with name, role and company.

How the layout changes with the browser size

The card has one fixed breakpoint: 768px of browser width (breakpoint-tablet). There is no separate tablet layout. From 768px up, the card fits its profile row to its own width, so the same rules apply in the full content column, on a tablet and in a narrow column.

Browser width Card width Padding Closed card Open card Button
Desktop, 1024px and up 912px at 1024px, growing to 1140px (content-max) from 1252px 24px (spacing-xl) Profiles on one row, by the profile rule Everyone in two columns with name, role and company At the right end of the profile row; beside the title when there are no profiles
Tablet, 768–1023px 696–951px (the browser less the 36px page margins) 24px The same row. The card is narrower, so names split and profiles stack sooner (see the next table) Two columns The same
Mobile, under 768px The browser less the 20px page margins 16px (spacing-rg) One column: every profile under the last, name and company only. No headshot stack and no "+N" One column; roles are added Full width, at the bottom of the card
  • The breakpoint follows the browser, not the card. A card in a narrow column on a desktop page keeps the row layout and fits it to that column.
  • Time, title (24px, two lines at most) and chevron keep their size and place at every width.

Between 768px and full width: how the row fits

A closed card keeps its profiles on one row. When the row is too wide for the card, it changes in this order, and changes back as the card widens:

  1. Full names on one line (four or five profiles).
  2. First name over surname.
  3. Profiles move into the headshot stack one at a time, last first. "+N" keeps count.

One to three profiles never stack: they stay in equal columns and the role stops at two lines. Nothing overlaps or wraps to a second row.

These steps have no fixed breakpoints: the card measures its row, so the widths depend on how long the names are. With the sample names (9 to 18 characters), a closed card shows the following. "With a button" means a 136px button (Register or Join Waitlist).

Profiles Card 1140px (desktop) Card 950px (tablet, landscape) Card 700px (tablet, portrait) Card 560px (half column)
1 to 3 All named: name, role, company The same The same The same; roles wrap to two lines
4 4 named, names on one line 4 named, one line 4 named, names on two lines. With a button: 3 named, 1 stacked 3 named, 1 stacked. With a button: 2 named, 2 stacked
5 5 named, one line 5 named, two lines 4 named, 1 stacked. With a button: 3 named, 2 stacked 3 named, 2 stacked. With a button: 1 named, 4 stacked
6 6 named. With a button: 4 named, 2 stacked The same 4 named, 2 stacked. With a button: 2 named, 4 stacked 2 named, 4 stacked. With a button: 1 named, 5 stacked
8 4 named, 4 stacked The same 3 named, 5 stacked. With a button: 2 named, 6 stacked 2 named, 6 stacked. With a button: 1 named, 7 stacked

Where each change starts, without a button (a button takes about 156px with its gap, so add that):

  • 4 profiles: names split under about 780px; stacking starts under about 600px.
  • 5 profiles: names split under about 960px; stacking starts under about 740px.
  • 6 profiles: stacking starts under about 880px.
  • More than 6: the fourth named profile joins the stack under about 740px.

Sizes and usage

  • Width: the card fills its container; there is no maximum. It is designed for the 1140px column. Minimum 320px; with a button on a screen of 768px or wider, keep it at least 420px wide, or the row cannot fit one name, the stack and the button.
  • Height follows the content. Closed, with the sample content: 105px with no profiles, 168 to 209px with profiles. On mobile a closed card grows by about 62px per profile (615px with eight).
  • Use the full-width column for agendas where most sessions have four or more speakers. In a column under about 560px only two profiles are named.
  • For long agendas on mobile, set speakerVisibility="open-only" so closed cards stay short, and let the open card list the speakers.
  • When profiles are stacked, turn on profileCards so each headshot can still give its name.

  • The row is fitted again whenever the card changes width and when the web fonts finish loading.

  • CTA: closed, it sits at the right of the profile row, on its last line. Open, it takes the empty cell on the last row, or a row of its own at the right when the rows are full; with one or two profiles it stays beside them.

  • Button width: every card button is at least 136px wide, the width of the longest standard label, Join Waitlist (133px). Register (red, secondary) and Join Waitlist (blue, secondary-alt) are then the same size and line up down a list. Keep card labels to two short words; a longer label makes its button wider than the rest.
  • Mobile CTA: the button spans the card at the bottom. layout="mobile" shows the phone layout at any screen width (the preview uses it).
  • The whole header is the toggle (a heading with a button, aria-expanded); the CTA is a separate control, so clicking it doesn't open the card. The headshot stack reads "and N more" to screen readers.
  • For a list of sessions, use Accordion variant="cards": it stacks the cards 16px apart and opens one at a time.
  • From the review rounds: no extra-large avatars; names use the title styles with a tight gap to role and company.
  • Figma's CTA here is a 48px outlined red button; the system's secondary Button is 50px, so cards with a CTA run 2px taller than the Figma frames.
  • The profile rule was set in review. Figma lets one to three profiles sit at their own width, which pushed long roles onto extra rows; here they take equal columns and the role stops at two lines.
  • Shown only when open: ctaVisibility and speakerVisibility are "always" (the default) or "open-only". With open-only the closed card leaves that part out and it appears when the card opens. Use it to keep a long agenda compact.
  • Profile hover cards: profileCards turns every headshot into a button that opens a profile HoverCard: headshot, name, role, the company logo (the speaker's logo) and the LinkedIn button (from the speaker's link), with the close icon top right. Pointing at a headshot peeks at its card; clicking pins it, and the other headshots wait until it is closed.

Components

Overlays and messages

Modal

Component

The base modal: small, medium and large, with or without a footer; then mobile. The button opens a live one.

Usage notes

The base dialog: a title with a close button, a body, and an optional footer of buttons. The other modals in this file are built on it.

Provide: open, onClose, title and the body as children. Optionally actions (a list of { label, onClick, variant, href }, or your own buttons), size, eyebrow, subtitle.

  • Sizes: sm 480px, md 540px (default), lg 600px. The height follows the content; past the viewport the body scrolls and the title and footer stay put.
  • Panel: white, radius-lg, shadow-modal, 24px padding, centred on an Overlay.
  • Title: h4 (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 20px; h3, 24px, on lg), text-primary. A 1px stroke-neutral-400 line sits under it, inset 24px.
  • Body: IBM Plex Sans Regular 16px, text-secondary.
  • Footer: buttons on the right, 12px apart, the primary one last. In actions the last item is primary unless you set variant.
  • Close: the cross top right (44px tap area), Esc, or a press on the backdrop. closeOnOverlay={false} keeps the backdrop from closing it; dismissible={false} removes all three, so the footer must offer a way out.
  • Mobile: 12px from the screen edges; the buttons stack full width with the primary on top.
  • Motion: fades in and grows from 95% over 200ms; no motion under reduced-motion settings.
  • Accessibility: role="dialog" named by the title. Focus moves into the modal, stays inside, and returns to what opened it. The page behind doesn't scroll. initialFocus takes a selector when something other than the first control should get focus.
  • overlay="dark" uses the 50% backdrop. inline draws the panel in the page flow with no backdrop, for documentation.
  • Figma puts the primary button on the left in the small and medium modals and on the right in the large one; this puts it on the right everywhere.
  • Figma's shadow is 0 16px 32px at 10%; this uses shadow-modal.

AlertDialog

Component

A decision that must be answered: destructive, warning and info; then mobile.

Usage notes

A decision that has to be answered before anything else: delete, leave without saving, reload.

Provide: open, title, message, and either onConfirm and onCancel (with confirmLabel and cancelLabel) or your own actions. tone picks the colour.

  • Tones: destructive (red bar, warning triangle), warning (amber bar), info (blue bar). The icon sits in a 50px disc on a 10% tint of the same colour.
  • 440px wide, centred text: title h4 (SemiBold 20px), message Regular 14px text-secondary, a full-width line, then the two buttons centred, secondary first.
  • It can't be dismissed. No close button, Esc does nothing and the backdrop does nothing: one of the buttons must be pressed.
  • Mobile: 12px from the screen edges; buttons stack full width, the primary on top.
  • Accessibility: role="alertdialog", named by the title and described by the message. Focus starts on the first button, which is the safe one (Cancel).
  • Say what happens in the title and name the action on the button ("Delete", not "OK").
  • The warning bar uses utility-warning-default. Figma draws it #f5a624 here and #f29912 elsewhere in the same file.

Overlay

Component

The backdrop behind a modal: 25% by default, 50% when the page behind is busy.

Usage notes

The backdrop behind a modal, from the Figma Modals, Popups & Tooltips file. Every modal in this system draws its own, so you only need this one when you build a new kind of layer.

Provide: nothing for the default. tone="dark" for the stronger one; onClick to hear a press on the backdrop itself; inline to keep it inside a positioned box instead of covering the screen.

  • Light: black at 25% (overlay-light), the default. Dark: black at 50% (overlay-dark), for a busy page or media behind.
  • Fixed to the viewport at z-overlay; fades in over 200ms, with no motion under reduced-motion settings.
  • The page behind stays visible but out of reach: it doesn't scroll and can't be clicked.
  • Empty, it is hidden from assistive technology.
  • Figma's layout frames use Charcoal at 25% instead of black; this follows the Overlay component itself.
  • ProfileModal and FilterDrawer were drawn earlier with a 70% backdrop and keep it for now.

Toast

Component

A short message over the page: success, warning, error, info. Fades in; Show again replays.

Usage notes

A short message that appears over the page without taking focus. Use ToastStack to place and time them.

Provide: status and the message. onClose adds the dismiss button.

  • Status: success (green, tick), warning (amber), error (red, cross in a circle), info (blue, the default).
  • 400px wide and at least 80px tall, white, radius-rg, shadow-modal, with a 4px stripe in the status colour down the left edge.
  • Icon: a 30px rounded tile on a 10% tint of the status colour.
  • Message: IBM Plex Sans Regular 14px, text-secondary. One or two lines; it wraps and the toast grows.
  • Dismiss: a 16px cross with a 44px tap area.
  • Motion: a toast fades in over 300ms when it appears. In a ToastStack it also rises 12px as it fades. It appears at once for people who prefer reduced motion.
  • Accessibility: success and info are role="status" and read out politely; warning and error are role="alert" and read out at once.
  • The colour is never the only signal: the icon changes with the status too.
  • Don't put the only route to an action in a toast, since it goes away by itself.

ToastStack

Pattern

Where toasts appear: bottom left, three at most, each leaving by itself. Press the buttons to add some.

Usage notes

Where toasts live: a corner of the screen, three at most, each leaving by itself.

Provide: items ({ id, status, message }) and onDismiss(id), which you answer by removing that item from your list.

  • Place: bottom left by default, 36px from the bottom and in line with the page margin; position also takes bottom-right, top-left and top-right. On mobile it spans the screen with 12px margins.
  • Order: the newest sits at the bottom, 12px apart.
  • Three at most (max). With more, the newest three show and the older ones return as space frees up.
  • Timing: success and info leave after 5 seconds, warnings after 8, errors stay until dismissed. Set duration on an item to change it (0 keeps it).
  • The timer pauses while the pointer is over a toast.
  • Motion: each one fades in and rises 12px over 300ms; no motion under reduced-motion settings.
  • Sits at z-toast, above every modal.
  • Accessibility: the stack is a region named "Notifications" and never takes focus. Each toast announces itself.
  • inline draws the stack in the page flow, for documentation.
  • Figma draws toasts bottom left while its notes say they "stack from top"; this follows the drawing.

Tooltip

Component

A short label on hover or focus: top, bottom, left and right, dark and light. The last row is live.

Usage notes

A short label for the thing it points at, shown on hover and on keyboard focus.

Provide: label and the element it describes as the child. Optionally position and theme.

  • Position: top (default), bottom, left, right, with a small arrow pointing at the trigger, 8px away.
  • Theme: dark (white text on surface-neutral-600, the default) or light (white with a hairline and shadow-modal), for dark backgrounds.
  • 8px by 12px padding, radius-sm, IBM Plex Sans Medium 14px, up to 240px wide before it wraps.
  • Timing: appears 300ms after the pointer arrives and at once on keyboard focus; fades over 150ms. delay changes the wait.
  • Leaves when the pointer leaves, when focus moves on, or on Esc.
  • Sits at z-tooltip.
  • Accessibility: role="tooltip", tied to the trigger with aria-describedby. Plain text as the child gets a dotted underline and a tab stop so the keyboard can reach it.
  • A few words only, and never the only place something important is said: it can't be reached on touch screens. No links or buttons inside.
  • open forces it on, for documentation.
  • Figma sets the text at 13px; this uses 14px, the smallest size in the type scale. Figma's 8px corner uses radius-sm.

HoverCard

Component

A small card on hover, click or tap: a logo card and a profile card. The last row is live.

Usage notes

A small card that opens beside the thing it describes. Use it where a logo or a headshot stands for something that needs a line of explanation and one link. Two kinds: the logo card (Figma: Hover card) and the profile card.

Provide: kind (logo or profile), the content for that kind, and the trigger as the child.

  • Logo card (kind="logo"): logo (and logoAlt), optional badge (an image address or your own node, for a partner or certification badge), title, body and link ({ label, href }). The link is a neutral TextLink with the blue arrow. One link only.
  • Profile card (kind="profile", Figma: Profile Modal - Alternate): name (the full name), image (falls back to the avatar silhouette), designation (the role), company, logo (the company logo, with logoAlt) and link ({ href }). Layout: the 56px headshot (Avatar md) on the left, 16px from the text; the name, then the role 4px under it; a foot row 16px below with the company logo on the left (28px tall, up to 140px wide; the company name in Medium when there is no logo) and the LinkedIn button on the right (SocialButton size="sm": 36px, radius-sm, a 20px white glyph on icon-bg-default). The close icon (24px in a 32px target, icon-default) sits 8px from the top and right (spacing-3xs), so its glyph lines up with the 16px padding. The link opens in a new tab.
  • Size: logo card 242px wide; profile card 400px wide; both 16px padding (spacing-rg), radius-lg, white, shadow-modal. Never wider than the screen less 16px each side. Height follows the content: keep the copy to three lines.
  • Type: logo card: name h4 (20px SemiBold), copy paragraph-rg text-secondary. Profile card: the profile text used everywhere (see Avatar): name title-sm (SemiBold 16px), role paragraph-rg text-secondary, company in Medium. Long names wrap; nothing is cut off.
  • Opens: a mouse opens it on hover after 150ms and it stays open while the pointer is on the trigger or the card. A click, a tap or Enter opens it and keeps it open. Focus alone does not open it, so tabbing through a row of logos stays quiet.
  • Closes: when the pointer leaves (200ms grace) if hover opened it; on a click outside, on Esc, on the close icon, or on a second click of the trigger. Opened from the keyboard, focus moves into the card and returns to the trigger when it closes; Tab past the last control closes it.
  • One profile card at a time: a profile card opened with a click, a tap or the keyboard is pinned. It stays open when people click elsewhere, and the other headshots don't open theirs (no hover, no click, default cursor) until it is closed with the close icon, Esc or a second click of its own headshot.
  • Position: 8px below the trigger, centred on it (align="start" or "end" lines it up with an edge). It moves above when there is no room below (position="top" asks for that first) and is kept 16px inside the screen. It sits at z-tooltip.
  • Cursor: pointer on the trigger. The trigger is a button; if the child is not a button or link, HoverCard wraps it in one and names it ": details" (triggerLabel overrides).
  • Mobile: the same card, opened by a tap; a tap outside or the close icon closes it. Set closable on a logo card that will be used on touch screens.
  • In the logo modules: give a logo a card in LogoCarousel or LogoHierarchy and the logo becomes the trigger. The carousel waits while a card is open.
  • On headshots: DrawerCard takes profileCards to give every speaker headshot a profile card.
  • Accessibility: the trigger has aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; the card is a dialog labelled by its name. A tooltip is for a few words of plain text; a hover card is for content with a link.
  • inline draws the card in the page flow without a trigger, for documentation.
  • Partner logos and badges in the preview are placeholders.

CookieBanner

Pattern

Cookie consent: the compact bar and the preferences panel; then mobile.

Usage notes

Cookie consent in two forms: a compact bar along the bottom of the screen, and a panel with a switch for each category.

Provide: for the bar, onAccept and onDecline, plus link for the policy and onManage to open the panel. For the panel, variant="expanded", categories ({ id, label, description, required }), onSave(prefs) and onAccept(prefs).

  • Compact: fixed to the bottom at full width, white with shadow-modal. A 24px cookie icon, the message in 14px text-secondary with a "Learn more" link, then Decline (secondary) and Accept All (primary), both small. It slides up over 400ms.
  • Expanded: a 600px panel on an Overlay: "Cookie Preferences" (h4, SemiBold 20px), a line of copy, then one Toggle per category with its name (Medium 14px) and description, and Save Preferences and Accept All at the bottom left.
  • A required category is switched on and can't be changed.
  • onSave gets the choices as { id: true | false }; onAccept gets every category as true.
  • It stays until answered. Neither form has a close button, and Esc and the backdrop do nothing.
  • The bar doesn't block the page; the panel does, and keeps focus inside.
  • Mobile: the bar stacks with full-width buttons; the panel becomes a sheet from the bottom with its buttons stacked.
  • Sits at z-cookie: above the page and tooltips, below modals.
  • Accessibility: the bar is a region named "Cookie consent"; the panel is a dialog named by its title.
  • Figma's notes say Accept All and Decline "must be equally prominent", but both drawings show a secondary and a primary button. This follows the drawings.

ExitIntent

Pattern

A last offer as someone leaves: with an image, or centred on a resource; then mobile.

Usage notes

A last offer shown as someone moves to leave the page: one field and one button.

Provide: open, onClose, title, subtitle and onSubmit(value). type="offer" (default) takes an image; type="content" takes an icon.

  • Offer: 600px wide, a 220px image down the left and the content on the right: title h4 (SemiBold 20px), subtitle 14px, the field, a full-width primary button, then the "No Thanks" link with its arrow.
  • Content: 480px wide and centred, with a 64px icon tile (radius-md, 10% blue) above the title, for a report or guide.
  • The field is Work Email by default; change it with field ({ name, label, type }). An empty or malformed address shows the error under the field and keeps the modal open.
  • Dismissing: the cross, Esc, the backdrop or the "No Thanks" link (onDismiss, otherwise onClose).
  • Mobile: 12px from the screen edges; the image is dropped and the text is centred.
  • Accessibility: role="dialog". Focus starts on the close button, so leaving is always one key away.
  • This component only draws the modal. Decide when to open it yourself, show it once per visit, and never over another modal.
  • submitLabel and dismissLabel replace the default wording.
  • Ground: the panel sits on the form ground, surface-neutral-200, the same as Form; the field stays white.

SessionTimeout

Pattern

The warning with a countdown, then the signed-out notice; then mobile.

Usage notes

The warning before someone is signed out, with a live countdown, and the notice once they have been.

Provide: open, onStay, onSignOut and onSignIn (or signInHref). Give defaultSeconds and it counts down by itself and calls onExpire; or pass seconds to drive the clock yourself.

  • Warning: 56px amber disc, "Session Expiring Soon", one line of copy, the time left, then Log Out (secondary) and Stay Signed In (primary) side by side.
  • Clock: IBM Plex Sans Medium 32px in warning-strong, on an 8% amber tint, radius-rg. It updates every second.
  • Expired: a grey disc, "Session Expired" and one full-width Sign In Again button. It switches to this at zero, or straight away with state="expired".
  • 440px wide, 24px padding, everything centred.
  • It can't be dismissed. No close button, no Esc, no backdrop click.
  • Show it five minutes before the session ends (300 seconds is the default).
  • Mobile: 12px from the screen edges, 16px padding; buttons stack with Stay Signed In on top.
  • Accessibility: role="alertdialog". The clock is a timer, so it isn't read out every second. Focus starts on Stay Signed In, so Enter never signs anyone out by accident.
  • Every label and line of copy can be replaced: title, message, expiredTitle, expiredMessage, stayLabel, signOutLabel, signInLabel.
  • Figma's mobile drawing puts the secondary button on top; here the primary is on top, as in the other mobile dialogs.

SuccessConfirmation

Pattern

The confirmation after an action: general and download; then mobile.

Usage notes

The "it worked" notice after an action: a green tick, a line of copy and one button.

Provide: open, onClose. Optionally title, message, actionLabel and onAction; type="download" with href for a file.

  • General: "Success!" with a Done button that closes it.
  • Download: "Download Ready" with a Download Now button; with href the button is a download link.
  • 440px wide, centred: a 64px disc on a 10% green tint with the tick in utility-success-default, title h4 (SemiBold 20px), message 14px text-secondary, one full-width primary button.
  • Closes with the button, Esc or the backdrop. There is no cross.
  • Mobile: 12px from the screen edges, 16px padding.
  • Accessibility: role="dialog", named by the title and described by the message. Focus starts on the button.
  • For something that needs no reply, use a success Toast instead; this one stops the page.

Components

Media

Media

Component

The media slot the modules share: image placeholder, a photo, and a video with the play button.

Usage notes

The image or video slot the block modules share: Hero, GeneralContent, TabModule, AccordionModule and CtaModule all take a media prop and draw it with this.

Provide: src and alt for an image; video and poster for a video. With neither it shows the Figma placeholder.

  • radius-lg, and the picture always covers the box. Set the shape with ratio (for example "16 / 9"); inside a module the module sets it.
  • Video: the poster with a 64px white play button, its triangle in Asphalt. If video is a file address, pressing play swaps the poster for the player with its controls. Pass video={true} and handle onPlay to open a modal instead.
  • Placeholder: surface-neutral-400 with the image glyph in Rhino; a video placeholder is Asphalt.
  • Give the play button a name with playLabel when "Play video" isn't specific enough.
  • Write alt text that says what the picture shows; leave it empty for decoration.

Page modules

Header and footer

Nav

Page module

Global navigation: mega menu, a dropdown for every other item, Community bar, mobile menu.

Usage notes

The global navigation from the Figma Navigation page: the logo, the primary items with their menus, utility links, search and one call to action. Below 1200px it becomes a bar with a menu button that opens a full-screen menu.

Provide: logoSrc (the full-colour logo from Logos), items, utility links, search and cta ({ label, href }). An item is a link ({ label, href }) or opens a menu ({ label, menu }).

Menu Give it Looks like
Mega menu menu: { overview, railLabel, groupsLabel, groups } A warm rail with the overview and a filter list, beside the groups of links in three columns
Column dropdown menu: { columns: [{ title, links }] } One or more titled columns of large links

Desktop bar (1200px and up)

  • White, 80px tall, shadow-nav. Content is 1140px wide and centred.
  • Logo 37px tall, then 36px to the items. Items and utility links are IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-primary, 16px apart; they turn text-accent-primary on hover.
  • The current or open item shows a 4px qualys-blue bar on the bottom edge of the nav. Set it with current (the item's label). It is one bar for the whole row: tapping another item slides it across (300ms ease-in-out, the same motion as Tabs), and closing a menu sends it back to the current page. With reduced motion it moves without sliding.
  • Right side: a 16px search icon (see Search panel), the utility links ("Community", "Login", "Contact Us") and a small primary Button ("Get Started"), each 16px apart.
  • Narrow desktop (1200–1365px): utility links marked collapse: true hide, so the row keeps its spacing. On qualys.com mark Community and Contact Us; Login, search and Get Started always stay. Both stay in the mobile menu and the footer.
  • Menus open on hover and on click, Enter or Space. Esc, a click outside or moving the pointer away closes them. hover={false} makes them click-only.
  • Menus slide open downwards from under the bar (300ms ease-in-out) and slide shut the same way (250ms). Moving from one open menu to the next only fades, so the panel doesn't drop twice.

Desktop menus: one type and spacing scale

Both menu kinds use the same sizes, so moving between Platform, Solutions and the rest feels like one menu:

Role Style Spacing
Eyebrow ("PLATFORM APPS", "PARTNERS") eyebrow-xs 12px, text-secondary 12px down to its stroke-neutral-500 rule, 20px from the rule to the content
Overview title, group headings, capability filter rows, column-dropdown links Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 16px 12px from a heading to its links
Group links IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px, text-secondary 16px (spacing-rg) between links; 32px between groups
Description IBM Plex Sans Regular 16px 4px under the overview title
New and other badges Tag sm (tag-xs 12px Bold, 25px tall) 8px after the last word. A badge labels, it never asks: "New", not "Discover" or "Try"
Panel radius-lg, shadow-card 24px top and bottom, 36px at the sides (24px in the rail)

Mega menu

  • 1249px wide, centred under the bar.
  • Rail: 300px, surface-neutral-200. The overview eyebrow, title and description; 24px below, a second eyebrow and the filter list: "All" plus one row per group, at least 44px tall (10px × 12px padding), with no gap between rows, so a hovered row sits right against the active one. Choosing a row shows only that group.
  • Groups: an eyebrow over a rule, then three columns 32px apart, filled in order down each column (Risk Operations Center, Vulnerability & Configuration Management and Compliance first). groupColumns: 2 gives two columns for a menu with fewer, longer groups. On hover a link turns text-accent-primary and a 16px qualys-blue arrow slides in beside it.
  • Long labels: a link that wraps onto two lines keeps its arrow (and its New badge) after the last word, not beside the whole block. The last word, badge and arrow never break apart.
  • badge: true on a group or link adds a small blue "New" Tag; pass a string for other wording.

Hover, everywhere in the Nav: the label turns text-accent-primary. Links inside a menu (group links, linked group headings, the overview title, column links) also get the blue arrow sliding in from the left over 150ms. The filter rows in the rail are buttons, not links, so they tint instead.

Column dropdown

  • Each column is 340px: an eyebrow over a rule, then links 16px apart. They hover like the mega menu's links: blue label, blue arrow.

Search panel

  • With search set and no href or onClick, the search icon opens a panel under the bar, like a menu: the width of the bar's content (1140px), radius-lg, shadow-card, 24px × 36px padding.
  • Inside: a contained SearchBar (56px) that takes focus as the panel opens, and optional suggestions below it under a "Popular searches" eyebrow, as tag chips (the FilterChip style, 36px, 8px apart) that link to their results.
  • While it is open the icon becomes a cross and the blue bar sits under it. The cross, Esc or a click outside closes it, and focus returns to the icon. Pressing Enter calls onSearch with the query.
  • Unlike the menus, it doesn't close when the pointer leaves, and hovering an item doesn't swap it for that item's menu: someone may be typing.
  • Mobile: the menu panel already starts with the search field, so there is no separate panel.

Mobile and tablet (below 1200px)

  • A 64px bar with the logo and a menu button. It opens a full-screen white menu with the logo and a close button on top.
  • First level: a contained SearchBar, then one row per item (Medium 16px, a qualys-blue arrow, stroke-neutral-500 rules). The utility links (text-secondary) and a full-width primary Button sit at the bottom.
  • Drilling in: an item with a menu opens its own level. A mega menu shows the overview and the filter list as rows; choosing "All" or a group shows its links. The blue link at the top names the current level and goes back one step.
  • The menu slides in from the right edge and slides back out when it closes (300ms ease-in-out). Each level slides in from the side it came from: from the right when drilling in, from the left when going back.
  • Esc or the close button closes the menu and returns focus to the menu button; focus stays inside while it is open, and moves to the back link after each step.
  • With reduced motion, menus and levels appear and disappear without sliding.

Spacing, minimum and maximum

  • Don't tighten the menus further: 16px between links and 44px filter rows are the minimum for comfortable pointing, and the menus never use text below 16px, apart from eyebrows and badges. Keep group and link labels short: in three columns each is about 270px wide.
  • The panel is never taller than the window less 120px; past that it scrolls inside. The rail's warm ground always runs to the panel's bottom edge, including while it scrolls.

Community

  • label="COMMUNITY" adds the site name beside the logo (Wix Madefor Text Medium 18px) and align="center" centres the items in the remaining space. No utility links or call to action.

Notes

  • The Figma page is marked Pending Review and its usage notes are still "TBD", so expect changes.
  • The items and the Platform menu's names follow qualys.com: Platform, Solutions, Customers, Resources, Support, Partners, Company. Figma draws menus for Platform and Solutions only; the preview's other menus use the column dropdown with links and addresses from qualys.com's sitemap and footer, so their grouping is provisional.
  • Figma draws the hamburger bar for tablet (760px) and mobile; the switch is set at 1200px, where the full row stops fitting.
  • The Community bar has no tablet or mobile design; it uses the same mobile menu.
  • Mobile link text is drawn in #4D4D4D and desktop in Asphalt; both use text-secondary.
  • layout="desktop" or "mobile" forces one layout, and inlinePanel shows the mobile menu in the page flow, for documentation.
  • Shape: the bar runs edge to edge with square corners; only its menu panels are rounded (radius-lg).
  • Hover and active rows: in the mega menu's rail, hover is a neutral tint (chip-bg, 5% Charcoal) and the active row is Misty Blue (surface-blue-200) with the blue marker on its left edge. The same rule as the list AccordionModule and every list of tabs.

NavBanner

Page module

Event promotion above the navigation; the cross dismisses it.

Usage notes

The event promotion bar from the Figma Navigation page ("Event"): one line above the navigation announcing an event, with a link and a close button.

Provide: title ("Join your peers at ROCon"), optionally meta (the date and place, e.g. ['November 18-20', 'Mumbai']) and cta ({ label, href }).

  • 52px tall, full width, on the blue gradient (blue-gradient-end to blue-gradient-start and back). All text is text-inverted.
  • Title in Wix Madefor Text Medium 16px; the date and place in Medium 18px, separated by "|"; 36px; then an inverted TextLink with an arrow.
  • The copy is centred. A 24px cross sits 36px from the right edge and dismisses the bar; dismissible={false} hides it and onClose tells you when it was closed.
  • Shape: the banner and the navigation run edge to edge with square corners. Neither is ever drawn as a rounded card.
  • Use it for event promotion only, one at a time, placed directly above Nav.
  • On narrow screens the copy wraps and aligns left; Figma has no tablet or mobile design for this yet.
  • In Figma the navigation under the banner is an older mock (grey labels, a "Try Now" button); the standard Nav is used here.

NotificationBar

Page module

One line across the top of the page: info, success, warning and promo; then mobile.

Usage notes

One line across the top of the page for something everyone should know: maintenance, a release, an expiring licence, an event.

Provide: type and the message. Optionally link ({ label, href }) and onClose for the dismiss button.

  • Types: info (blue circle), success (green tick), warning (amber triangle), promo (party icon, usually with a link).
  • A white bar, radius-rg, at least 44px tall, set 16px in from the top and sides of the page, with a hairline in surface-neutral-300.
  • Message: IBM Plex Sans Medium 14px, text-primary, with a 16px icon before it. The link is a small blue TextLink with its arrow.
  • Dismiss: a 16px cross on the right, 44px tap area.
  • Mobile: 12px from the edges, 12px text; the message wraps and the link drops under it.
  • Place it above the Nav. It stays in the page flow and scrolls away with the page.
  • Accessibility: role="status"; a warning is role="alert" so it is read out at once.
  • One bar at a time. If it is dismissed, remember that for the visit.
  • NavBanner is the older announcement strip inside the Nav; use one or the other, not both.
  • The hairline isn't in Figma: it keeps the white bar visible on a white page.

Footer

Page module

Charcoal footer with the shield in a notch: lead copy, form, social and link columns.

Usage notes

The site footer from the Figma Footer file: Charcoal, with the Qualys shield in a raised notch, a lead block with a URL form and social links, three link columns and a centred legal line.

Provide: logoSrc (the shield from Logos), heading, body, form ({ placeholder, buttonLabel, action or onSubmit }), social ({ network, href, label }), columns ({ title, links }), copyright and legal links.

  • Ground: surface-neutral-600. A 402 × 40px notch rises from the top edge, centred; the shield (75px wide) sits 15px below it. Content is 1140px wide.
  • Rules: a 1px stroke-neutral-500 rule under the shield (48px below it, spacing-4xl) and another above the legal line.
  • Lead block (left, up to 512px): the heading in h3 (SemiBold 24px, text-inverted); 24px; the body in paragraph-md (18px) Rhino; 36px; the form; 36px; the social links.
  • Form: 472 × 54px, radius-rg, white at 20%, placeholder in white 16px. The submit button is 56 × 42px, button-bg-primary-default, radius-media (8px) corners, a chevron and a soft shadow; give it a buttonLabel for screen readers.
  • Social links: plain SocialButtons, 24px glyphs (lg) in Rhino, 44px touch targets 8px apart, white on hover. LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Vimeo and YouTube are in the Social Icons.
  • Link columns (right): 56px apart (spacing-5xl). Titles in IBM Plex Sans SemiBold 16px text-inverted; links in Medium 16px Rhino, 16px apart, white on hover.
  • Legal line: centred, paragraph-sm (14px) Rhino: the copyright, then each legal link followed by a full stop.
  • Tablet: the lead block stacks above the columns.
  • Mobile: a 303 × 31px notch with a 39px shield; 24px side margins (spacing-xl); the body drops to 16px; the form spans the width; the columns sit two across (12px between links) with a rule above them.
  • The footer follows its own width, so it also adapts inside a narrow container.

Where Figma's desktop and mobile frames disagree, one value is used for both:

  • Links, body copy and social glyphs are #BDBDBD on desktop and #B5B5B5, white and #D9DCE0 on mobile; all use Rhino.
  • The heading is Regular on desktop and SemiBold on mobile; it uses h3 (SemiBold).
  • The first mobile rule is drawn in #6A778B; it uses stroke-neutral-500 like the others.
  • In the mobile frame the heading overlaps the paragraph (its text box wasn't resized); here it takes the room it needs.

Page modules

Heroes and headers

Hero

Page module

Hero in each layout: split media, text only, on a photo or video, with a lead form; then mobile.

Usage notes

The top-of-page module from the Figma Hero page (Ready for Dev): an eyebrow, a display heading, a short paragraph and up to two actions, on its own, beside media, over a photo or video, or beside a lead form.

Provide: layout, size, eyebrow, title, body, actions, and for the layout: media (split), background (photo or video behind the copy), or form (a Form) with an optional visual.

Figma name Props Use it for
Split Media Impact / Standard Hero layout="split", media={{ src, alt }} or media={{ video, poster }} Product feature pages and service overviews, with a UI screenshot, lifestyle photo or demo video
Left-Aligned Text Impact / Standard Hero layout="left" Landing, category and index pages, where the message is text-heavy
Center-Aligned Impact / Standard Hero layout="center" Campaign, event and lead-generation pages, with brief, punchy copy
Left-Aligned Image Background Hero layout="left", background={{ src }} The same, over a full-bleed photo
Center-Aligned Image Background Hero layout="center", background={{ src }} The same, on a contained photo card
… Animation / Video background={{ video, src }} (src is the poster) A looping, silent background video
Lead Form Hero layout="form", form={{ … }}, visual Competitive and campaign pages that open with a sign-up

size="lg" is Impact (64px heading); size="rg" is Standard (56px).

Layout

  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom, content in the 1140px column (content-max).
  • Copy: eyebrow in eyebrow-xl (22px, text-secondary), 12px; the heading in display-xl (Impact) or display-lg (Standard), text-primary; 24px (Impact) or 16px (Standard); the body; 36px; the actions, 8px apart.
  • Body size: 24px (paragraph-lg) in the left-aligned and centred Impact heroes; 18px beside media or a form and in the centred Standard hero; 16px in the split Standard hero.
  • Split: copy up to 520px, 56px (spacing-5xl), media. Images are 14:9 (560 × 360) and videos 16:9, both radius-lg. Impact centres the copy on the media; Standard aligns both to the top.
  • Left and centre: the copy block is 1000px at most; centred heroes centre everything.
  • On a photo or video: radius-lg. tone: 'dark' (default) puts black at 50% over the picture, with white copy; tone: 'light' puts a white veil over it, with text-primary copy: 82% under centred copy; under left-aligned copy 92% fading to 30% at the far side, so the photo still shows there (a flat 86% on mobile). The left-aligned photo runs edge to edge with the copy on the 1140px column; centred photos and all videos sit in a 1140px card with 36px padding. Actions are a primary Button and an inverted TextLink with an arrow, 16px apart.
  • Lead form: copy on the left, the Form (variant="gate") on the right on surface-blue-100 with a deeper shadow. visual places a decorative graphic behind the form.

Tablet (768–1023px): split heroes stay side by side, copy 60% and media 40%, and the heading scales down. The lead form drops under the copy.

Mobile (under 768px): 24px × 20px padding. Media moves above the copy, 20px apart. Eyebrow 16px, heading 36px, body 18px (16px beside media or a form). Buttons stack full width, 8px apart. On a photo they keep their own width and stack 16px apart.

Character counts (from Figma)

Layout Headline Body
Split 40–60, under two lines on desktop 120–160
Left-aligned 50–75 150–200
Centred 30–50 100–140

Eyebrow: about 20 characters.

Do / Don't

  • Do keep one primary action; add a secondary Button or a TextLink only when there is a second step.
  • Do give every photo and poster alt text, or leave it empty when it is decoration.
  • Don't centre long headlines; use the left-aligned hero.
  • Prefer a pale, quiet picture for the light tone. The veil keeps dark copy readable on a busier photo, but it also washes the photo out. Figma draws white at 25%, which left the copy hard to read; raised in review.
  • Background video plays silent and looped, and stays on its poster when the reader asks for reduced motion.

Where the Figma frames disagree, one value is used:

  • The left-aligned photo hero is drawn with its copy 36px from the edge in the component, and on the 1140px column in the Layout Implementation frames; it uses the column.
  • In the Lead Form hero the star visual is drawn on top of the form; here it sits behind, so the form stays usable.
  • The mobile Standard split hero is drawn with a 32px heading; every mobile hero uses 36px.
  • The tablet frames squeeze the media to a sliver; here copy and media share the row 60/40.
