TypographicHeader

Page module

A section opener with no media: left-aligned and centred, then both on mobile.

Usage notes

The section opener from the Figma Typographic Headers page (Ready for Dev): an eyebrow, a heading, a short paragraph and up to two buttons, with no media.

Provide: title, and optionally eyebrow, body, actions and align="center".

  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom. The copy sits in a 1000px block, centred in the page.
  • Eyebrow: eyebrow-lg (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 18px, 5% letter spacing), text-secondary.
  • Heading: h2 (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 38px, line height 1.1, −2%), 6px under the eyebrow. It is an h2 unless you pass titleLevel.
  • Body: paragraph-rg (16px), 800px at most, 12px under the heading.
  • Actions: 32px under the body, 8px apart: a primary Button, then a secondary one.
  • align="center" centres the text, the paragraph block and the buttons.
  • Mobile: 24px × 20px padding; eyebrow 14px, heading 24px (h2 on mobile); the buttons stack full width, 24px under the body.

Use it to open a group of modules or cards. For the first heading on a page use Hero.

Notes:

  • Figma draws the heading Bold; it uses the closest heading style, h2 (SemiBold), like the General Content and Tab modules.
  • The left-aligned block starts 70px in from the 1140px column, because Figma centres a 1000px block. Say if it should line up with the column edge instead.
  • The mobile eyebrow is uppercase in Figma and mixed case on desktop; it is left as typed on both.
  • The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…").

Page modules

Content sections

GeneralContent

Page module

Copy beside an image or video, full-width media, and banners; then mobile. Videos play.

Usage notes

The general content module from the Figma General Content Modules page (Ready for Dev): copy beside an image or video, a full-width image or video, or a banner with the copy over the media.

Provide: layout, media, and for the copy eyebrow, title, body, actions.

Layout Figma name What it shows
media-right (default) Split Media Right Copy on the left, image or video on the right
media-left Split Media Left The same, mirrored
full Full width media / video The media alone, across the column
banner Full width … Type overlay Heading, one paragraph and a Button over the media

media is { src, alt } for an image or { video, poster } for a video; leave it empty to get the grey placeholder.

Split

  • Two equal columns, 48px apart, aligned to the top. Images are 8:5 and videos 16:9, radius-lg.
  • Copy: eyebrow in eyebrow-lg (text-secondary), 12px, the heading in h2 (SemiBold 38px), 12px, the body in paragraph-rg, 32px, the actions.
  • Actions, 8px apart, in any of the four Figma sets: a primary Button; primary and secondary; primary and a TextLink (tone="neutral", with the arrow); or the TextLink alone.

Full width

  • An image at 60:23 (1140 × 437) or a video at 16:9, radius-lg.

Banner

  • A radius-lg panel, 230px tall at least, 24px padding. The copy is 600px wide at most: heading in h2, 12px, the body, 24px, one primary Button, all in text-inverted.
  • A photo gets black at 50% over it. With no picture the panel is Asphalt.
  • A video banner adds the play button in the space right of the copy. If media.video is a file address, pressing play swaps the banner for the video player; otherwise handle media.onPlay.

Tablet (under 1024px): the split stacks, media first, 20px apart.

Mobile (under 768px): 24px × 20px padding; images 67:50, videos 16:9; eyebrow 16px, heading 24px (h2 on mobile); buttons stack full width with the TextLink centred under them. Banners get 16px padding and the play button moves to the bottom right corner.

Notes:

  • Figma draws the split at 1200px wide in the component and at 1140px in the page layouts; it uses the 1140px column like the other modules.
  • In the video banner Figma centres the play button on the panel, where it covers the end of the paragraph; it is moved clear of the copy.
  • The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…", "Image max width: 560px").

TabModule

Page module

A card with tabs across the top; each tab has its own copy and media. Click a tab.

Usage notes

The tab module from the Figma Tab Modules page: a white card with Tabs across the top, and under them a heading, copy, actions and media that change with the tab.

Provide: items — one per tab, each with label, title, body, actions and media — and optionally align="center" and label (what the tabs are, for screen readers).

  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom. The card is the 1140px column: surface-neutral-100, radius-lg, shadow-card, 36px padding.
  • Tabs: the Tabs component, at the top left, or centred with align="center". Use up to eight short labels; longer sets scroll sideways.
  • Content, 48px under the tabs: copy and media in two equal columns, 48px apart, centred on each other.
  • Copy: the heading in h2 (SemiBold 38px), 24px, the body in paragraph-rg, 24px, the actions, 8px apart. The Figma sets: a primary Button; primary and secondary; primary and a TextLink (tone="neutral", with the arrow).
  • Media: 16:9, radius-lg; an image, or a video with the play button.
  • Mobile: 24px card padding, 24px between the parts. The copy comes first and the media follows at 287:250. Buttons keep their own width and stack.
  • Switching tabs slides the blue bar and swaps the content. Arrow keys move between tabs.

Do / Don't:

  • Do keep every tab to the same structure, so the card doesn't jump in height.
  • Autoplay: autoplay passes straight to Tabs: the tabs advance every six seconds (or the time given), wait on hover and focus, stop when the reader picks a tab, and show a pause button beside the bar.
  • Don't put more than one primary Button in a tab.

The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…").

AccordionModule

Page module

An Accordion as a page section: full width, beside copy or media, or as a list. Click a row.

Usage notes

The accordion module from the Figma Accordion Modules page: an Accordion as a page section — under a heading, beside a copy block, beside media, or as a list with the open row's content beside it.

Provide: items (the same rows as Accordion: { id, title, icon, content, cta }) and a layout. Add title for the heading; eyebrow, body and actions for the copy block; media for the image or video. defaultOpen names the row that starts open. Give a row's cta as { label, href } and the module draws the right control (see Row CTA).

Layout Figma name Looks like
full Accordion Module, Full Width The heading, then the accordion across the 1140px column
split Split Content, CTA + Content Block Copy block on the left (eyebrow, heading, copy, up to two actions); accordion on the right
media-left Split Media Left Media on the left; accordion on the right. No heading
media-right Split Media Right Accordion on the left; media on the right. No heading
list The last frame (also labelled "Split Media Right") Rows on the left; the open row's content on the right
  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom, content in the 1140px column. Two-column layouts are two equal columns (546px), 48px apart, aligned at the top.
  • Heading: h2, SemiBold 38px, 36px above the accordion.
  • Copy block (split): eyebrow, 4px, heading, 16px, body in paragraph-rg, 32px, actions 8px apart. The Figma sets: a primary and a secondary Button; a primary Button and a TextLink (tone="neutral", with the arrow).
  • Rows: the standard Accordion (Drawer rows): Feature Icon, title, chevron; the open row shows its copy and a call to action. See Accordion and Drawer for sizes and limits (4 to 12 rows; every row has an icon or none).
  • Row CTA: a small primary Button. When the copy block already has a primary Button, and always in list, it is a TextLink instead (tone="neutral", with the arrow: charcoal label, blue arrow), so the module keeps one primary action. The module does this itself: a { label, href } CTA is drawn as whichever applies, and a primary Button passed as a node is redrawn as the TextLink. Other nodes are left as given.
  • Media: 546 × 460 with radius-lg; an image or a video. Supply images no wider than 560px (the one usage note Figma gives).
  • List: rows 56px tall in a 558px column, each with a 36px icon box 16px from the left edge. The open (active) row carries the blue Marker on its left edge and a chevron pointing at its content. There is one Marker for the list: it slides to the row you open, over 300ms, like the bar under the Nav links (it jumps for people who prefer reduced motion). marker={1}, {2} or {3} picks a flag-tier colour instead and marker={false} hides it; a row under the pointer is tinted (hyperlink-default at 15%). The content sits 56px to the right: body copy, then a TextLink 24px below. One row is always open — the first unless defaultOpen says otherwise — and opening another swaps the content.
  • Tablet and mobile (under 1024px): everything stacks 24px apart, in reading order: copy then accordion; media-left keeps the media first and media-right puts it last; under 768px the media is 67:50. list becomes an ordinary accordion. Rows follow Drawer's 48px mobile rows, and buttons in the copy block go full width under 768px.
  • Each row is a heading (one level below the module heading) holding a button with aria-expanded. In list the open row's button is aria-disabled, because it can't be closed.

Do / Don't:

  • Do use list when each row has more to say (two or three short paragraphs) and people will compare rows.
  • Do keep one primary Button in the module: with one in the copy block, rows end in a TextLink.
  • Don't put an accordion module directly after another one, or use it for fewer than four rows.

Where this differs from the Figma frames:

  • The split frames draw the accordion 561px wide, 15px past the column; here it fills its 546px column.
  • The full-width desktop frame leaves 32px under the last row where the others leave 48px; 48px is used.
  • Split media (media-left, media-right) has no heading, as in the Figma frames: leave out title, and let the media and the row titles carry the section. The mobile frame for full width drops the heading too; it is kept there.
  • Mobile row titles are 16px in these frames and 18px on the Accordion page; 18px is used, as in Accordion.
  • The split frames draw a small red Button inside the accordion next to the copy block's primary Button; here the row uses a TextLink, as asked in review.
  • In the list frame, one row has the chevron and another has the tint. Read as: chevron = the open row, tint = hover. The tint (#D9E7EF) is not on the colour sheets; hyperlink-default at 15% matches it within one step.
  • The Marker on the open list row is not in the Figma frame (added in review, in blue, sliding between rows); rows start 16px in rather than 8px to make room for it.
  • The list content ends in a TextLink on desktop and a small Button on mobile; here it is a TextLink at both sizes.
  • List rows, hover and active: hover is a neutral tint (chip-bg, 5% Charcoal). The open row is Misty Blue (surface-blue-200) with the blue marker on its left edge, which slides to the row over 300ms. The same rule as the navigation menu.
  • There are no tablet frames; the module stacks under 1024px like GeneralContent.

The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…", "Page types: product", "Character count: Heading, supporting copy").

Stats

Page module

Stats block (one panel) and stat cards three or four in a row, filled and outlined; then mobile.

Usage notes

The stats module from the Figma Stats page: three figures in one panel, or three or four StatCards in a row.

Provide: items — each with value, label, and optionally suffix, prefix, icon, description — plus layout and tone.

Layout Figma name Use it for
block (default) Stats Block Industry benchmarks, adoption rates and high-level facts that set the context
cards, three items Stats Card – 3 in a row Impact you enable: reductions, time saved, efficiency gains
cards, four items Stats Card – 4 in a row Mixed figures: counts, capabilities, rankings
  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom, content in the 1140px column.
  • Block: one radius-lg panel with 56px padding (spacing-5xl) and the figures 48px apart. tone="solid" (default) is the blue gradient (blue-gradient-start to blue-gradient-end) with white figures; tone="outline" is a 1px qualys-blue outline with blue figures.
  • Cards: StatCards 24px apart, large for three and medium for four. Solid cards are flat qualys-blue.
  • Each figure: a Feature Icon (56px), the number with its unit, the label and one line of description. See StatCard for the sizes.
  • Count up: every figure runs from 0 to its value once, when it first scrolls into view (1.2 seconds, easing out; not for people who prefer reduced motion). countUp={false} turns it off for the module. See StatCard.
  • Tablet: the panel tightens to 36px padding; cards wrap to two across.
  • Mobile: everything stacks, 24px apart, with 24px padding; numbers drop to 48px (38px for four).

Content, from the Figma usage notes:

  • Block: neutral and factual. Metric, then a brief descriptor: "70% of enterprises…". Avoid prescriptive language.
  • Three in a row: impactful and benefit-driven. Metric, then an action verb and the value: "Reduce", "Cut", "Accelerate".
  • Four in a row: balanced and clear; may mix counts ("50+ scripts"), speed ("50% faster") and platform figures ("1 agent").
  • Keep each figure's text under 120 characters.

Don't:

  • Don't mix solid and outlined cards in one row.
  • Don't use more than four figures in one module.

Page modules

Calls to action

CtaModule

Page module

The closing call to action: a sign-up form beside or over a picture, or a dark card.

Usage notes

The closing call to action from the Figma CTAs page: a sign-up form beside or over a picture, or a dark card with a heading and buttons.

Provide: form (Form props) and media with a layout; or, with no form, title, body and actions.

Layout Figma name What it shows
media-right (default with a form) CTA Form Module – Media Right The form on the left, a 14:9 image on the right
media-left CTA Form Module – Media Left The same, mirrored
bleed CTA Form Module – Media Bleed Right The picture runs off the right edge behind a rounded, cloud-shaped edge
background CTA Form Module – Media Full Bleed The picture fills the section under black at 50%; the form turns white
card (default without a form) CTA Module A dark card: heading, one paragraph, buttons

With a form

  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 56px top and bottom (spacing-5xl), content in the 1140px column.
  • The form is the Form component without its card (variant="full", appearance="bare"): the shield, a centred h2 heading, the fields, the opt-in, one primary Button and the consent line, 460px wide, centred in its half.
  • The image is radius-lg, 56px (spacing-5xl) from the form. media is { src, alt }; leave it empty for the placeholder.
  • Mobile: only the form shows, with 36px × 24px padding and a full-width button. The background picture stays behind it.

Card

  • 1140px, radius-lg, Asphalt, 48px padding, 32px above and below it.
  • Heading in h2, text-inverted; 16px; the body in paragraph-md (18px), 500px wide at most; 24px; the actions, 8px apart.
  • Mobile: 24px padding, heading 24px (h2 on mobile), body 16px, buttons stacked full width.

Do / Don't:

  • Do use one CtaModule per page, near the end.
  • Do give the picture alt text when it adds meaning; leave it empty when it is decoration.
  • Don't use the background layout over a busy picture; the fields need a calm ground.

Where the Figma frames disagree, one value is used:

  • The card's second button is drawn as a red outline on the grey card, which is hard to read (about 2:1). Use variant="secondary-inverted" (white outline) there.
  • Fields are drawn 50px tall; they are 56px, as TextField.
  • Every mobile frame shows the plain form; the background layout keeps its picture on mobile.
  • The card is Asphalt in the documented example and Rhino in the component; Asphalt is used, because white text needs it.
  • The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…").

FormBanner

Page module

A heading band over a lead form: gradient, light or photo, with optional artwork on the right.

Usage notes

A lead form with a banner on top: a short heading on a coloured or photo band, and the Form attached under it in one card. Use it in the middle or at the foot of a page where the form needs its own headline. For a form at the top of the page use the Hero with a form; beside copy, use the CTA module.

Provide: title and form (the props of a Form, or a Form of your own). Optionally subtitle, background, tone and image.

  • Band background: gradient (the promo gradient, the default), light (surface-blue-200, Misty Blue) or a photo as { src }. A photo covers the band and is cropped from the centre; pick a dark, quiet one.
  • Heading colour (tone): inverted (white, the default on the gradient and on photos) or blue (text-accent-primary, the default on the light band). The heading is h3, 24px SemiBold, two lines at most; the optional subtitle is paragraph-rg.
  • Artwork: image sits on the right of the band, up to 460px wide and 150px tall, scaled to fit. Decorative, so it has no alt text unless imageAlt is given. Hidden on mobile.
  • Size: the card fills the 1140px content column; the band is at least 154px tall with 56px side padding (spacing-5xl) and grows with its text. radius-lg, shadow-card.
  • Form: sits on the form ground (surface-neutral-200) with 36px padding (spacing-3xl). It is the extended Form by default: its own 24px heading and subtitle, fields, one primary Button, the consent line. Mark fields half: true to pair them in a row.
  • Mobile (the module narrower than 768px): the band keeps its heading with 16px side padding, the artwork goes, fields stack in one column and the button fills the width.
  • States, validation and messages are the Form's own. One primary Button in the module.
  • Accessibility: the banner heading is an h2 by default (titleLevel changes it) and the form heading is one level below it.
  • From the test site's Form Banner. The test site draws the form with the old Marketo skin; Flex uses the Flex Form.

Page modules

Carousels and logos

Carousel

Page module

Cards you scroll sideways, several at once or one across, with progress bar and arrows.

Usage notes

The carousel module from the Figma Carousel Modules page: a row of cards you scroll sideways, with a progress bar and previous / next buttons.

Provide: the cards as children, a label that names the set ("Latest resources"), and optionally variant="single" or slideWidth.

Variant Figma name What it shows
multi (default) Multi Card Carousel Cards 350px wide, 24px apart; three fit the column and the next one peeks in
single Single Card Carousel One card as wide as the 1140px column, such as a featured EventCard
  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom. The first card starts on the 1140px column and the row runs off the right edge of the page.
  • Controls, 36px under the cards and right-aligned to the column: the progress bar, 48px, then the two buttons.
  • Progress bar: 377 × 4px, Charcoal at 20% with a qualys-blue fill that grows as you move through the set.
  • Buttons: 48px, radius-rg, white with a hairline and a soft shadow, a 16px chevron each. The one that can't go further fades to 40%.
  • Cards in a row share the tallest height.
  • Mobile: cards 300px wide, 16px apart, starting 20px from the edge; the progress bar spans the width and the buttons sit centred, 24px below it.

Behaviour:

  • Swipe, drag the trackpad, or use the buttons; each press moves one card and cards snap into place.
  • The row can take keyboard focus and then scrolls with the arrow keys. Links inside cards stay reachable by Tab.
  • It never moves by itself.

Do / Don't:

  • Do use it for four or more cards of one kind. For three or fewer, use a grid.
  • Don't mix card types in one row.
  • Don't hide anything essential past the first screen; a carousel is for browsing.

Notes:

  • Figma's mobile "single" frame reuses the multi-card frame; here single cards stay one per screen on mobile too.
  • The buttons use shadow-dropdown and stroke-neutral-400, the closest tokens to the drawn hairline and shadow.
  • The Figma usage notes are still placeholders ("Used for…").

TestimonialCarousel

Page module

Testimonial cards in a carousel: large, on a photo, small and with video. Placeholders.

Usage notes

The testimonial modules from the Figma Testimonials page: TestimonialCards in a Carousel.

Provide: items (TestimonialCard props) and size.

Size Figma name Card width
lg (default) Large Testimonial Card Carousel 939px; add image to each item for the photo version
sm Small Testimonial Card Carousel 500px, two and a bit across
video Video Testimonial Card Carousel 836px, with video on each item
  • Section on surface-neutral-200 with 100px above and below (the other carousels use 48px).
  • Cards 24px apart, starting on the 1140px column and running off the right edge; the next card peeks in.
  • Progress bar and buttons as in Carousel, right-aligned, 36px under the cards.
  • Tablet: large and video cards become as wide as the column and the large quote drops to 24px.
  • Mobile: 24px × 20px padding; every card is 300px wide, 16px apart; controls stack and centre.

Use it once per page. For a single quote, use a TestimonialCard on its own.

The logos in the preview are placeholders; use each customer's own logo file as they supply it.

LogoCarousel

Page module

A row of customer logos that scrolls by itself; pause by button or pointer. Placeholders.

Usage notes

The logo carousel from the Figma Logos page: a heading over one row of customer logos that scrolls by itself.

Provide: title and logos ({ src, alt, href, scale }). Optional: mobile, mobileMax, optical, duration.

  • Section on surface-neutral-100, 100px above and below.
  • Heading: h2 (SemiBold 38px), on the 1140px column, 740px wide at most. A 44px pause button sits at the right.
  • Logos, 56px (spacing-5xl) under the heading: tiles 200 × 80px, radius-md, 56px apart, each logo sized inside with 16px to spare. The row runs edge to edge and loops.

Mobile: stack or carousel

Below 768px the section takes 20px padding and the heading 24px. Choose what the logos do with mobile:

mobile What happens Use it when
stack (default) A still two-column grid, 36px between rows. Shows the first mobileMax logos (default 8) You have 8 logos or fewer, or a clear top 8
carousel The row keeps moving in smaller 144 × 56px tiles, 32px apart, with its pause button You have 9 or more logos and all of them matter

Stacking guidelines:

  • 8 logos at most (four rows of two). More than that pushes the content below too far down a phone screen.
  • Order the logos so the first 8 are the ones to keep: the extras are hidden on phones, not reshuffled.
  • Use an even number so the last row isn't half empty. mobileMax can be 4, 6 or 8.
  • With 9 or more logos that all need showing, use mobile="carousel".

Optical sizing

Logos are sized for equal visual weight, not equal width, as in LogoHierarchy: each gets about the same area in its tile (optical={false} turns this off). Each logo is centred in its tile; supply files cropped tight to the artwork, or a logo with padding on one side will look off-centre. Correct heavy or light logos with scale: 0.85–0.95 for dense, dark or boxed logos, 1.05–1.15 for thin or airy ones. See LogoHierarchy for the full guidance.

Behaviour

  • The row moves slowly to the left (about four seconds per logo; set duration in seconds to change it).
  • It pauses when the pointer is over it, when a logo link has focus, and when the pause button is pressed. The button then becomes play.
  • With reduced motion it doesn't move; the row can be scrolled instead.

Do / Don't

  • Do use each company's logo as supplied, on a clear ground.
  • Do give every logo alt text (the company name).
  • Don't use fewer than five logos; a short row has gaps as it loops.
  • Don't alter, recolour or crop a customer's logo. Adjust scale instead.

Notes

  • The pause control is drawn in Figma as a grey placeholder square; it uses the Carousel button style with a pause or play glyph.
  • Hover cards: give a logo a card ({ title, body, badge, link }) and it becomes a button that opens a logo HoverCard: on hover with a mouse, on click, tap or Enter otherwise. The row waits while a card is open. A logo with a card does not also take href; the link lives in the card.
  • The logos in the preview are placeholders.

LogoHierarchy

Page module

Logos in tiers under a heading: a lead sponsor, then rows of four. Placeholder logos.

Usage notes

The logo hierarchy from the Figma Logos page: logos grouped in tiers under a heading, such as event sponsors. The first tier (the signature sponsor) is drawn larger than the rest.

Provide: title and tiers — each with a label and logos ({ src, alt, href, scale }). Optional: a tier's level and mobileColumns, the module's mobileColumns and optical.

  • Section on surface-neutral-100, 100px above and below, everything centred.
  • Heading: h2 (SemiBold 38px) in text-secondary.
  • Tier: 36px under the heading or the tier before. The label is Wix Madefor Text Regular 20px text-secondary; 32px (spacing-2xl) below it, the logos.
  • Put the highest tier first with the fewest logos: one signature sponsor, then the standard sponsors.

Logo hierarchy

Level Desktop cell Mobile cell Use it for
signature 320 × 84px 240 × 64px The lead sponsor: one logo, two at most
standard 210 × 52px 143 × 35px Everyone else, four to a row on desktop, 32px apart (spacing-2xl), 48px between rows (spacing-4xl)
  • A first tier of one or two logos (with more tiers below) is the signature tier by default. Set level on a tier to override it.
  • The signature logo is about 1.5× the standard logos, enough to read as the lead without crowding the tier below.
  • Don't give a tier of three or more logos the signature level: it stops reading as a hierarchy.

Mobile columns

Below 768px the section takes 20px padding, the heading 24px and the labels Medium 18px. Standard sponsors stack in one or two columns; the signature tier is always one column.

Logos in the tier mobileColumns Why
1–4 1 One per row, 143 × 35px, 32px apart. Each logo stays big enough to read
5–12 2 Two per row, 32px between rows. Keeps the list to six rows or fewer
More than 12 2, or curate The tier gets long on a phone: show the top 12, or use LogoCarousel
  • auto (the default) picks 1 for up to four logos and 2 from five.
  • Set it per tier (tiers[i].mobileColumns) or for the module (mobileColumns).
  • Keep the same column count for tiers of the same level, so the page doesn't change rhythm halfway down.

Optical sizing

Logos come in very different shapes, so fitting each one to the full cell makes square and stacked marks look small and long wordmarks look loud. The module sizes them for equal visual weight instead.

  1. Equal area (automatic). Each logo gets about the same area inside its cell: a long wordmark runs wide and short, a square mark stands taller and narrower. On by default; optical={false} turns it off and fits every logo to the cell.
  2. Weight adjustments (by hand). Area doesn't account for ink. Use a logo's scale to correct it: - Dense, dark, filled or boxed logos (solid backgrounds, heavy type) look bigger: scale 0.85–0.95. - Thin, light or airy logos (hairline type, outlines, lots of white space) look smaller: scale 1.05–1.15. - Stay inside 0.8–1.2. If a logo needs more, the file has extra padding: ask for a tightly cropped version.
  3. Check against the neighbours. Squint or blur the row: no logo should jump out or sink back. Compare cap heights of wordmarks and the visual mass of symbols, not their boxes.

Supplying logo files:

  • Each logo is centred in its cell, both ways. A logo that looks off-centre has uneven padding in its file: crop it tight rather than nudging it.
  • SVG, cropped tight to the artwork with no padding, one colour version per ground (full colour or one-colour charcoal on light grounds).
  • Use the horizontal lockup where the brand has one; a stacked lockup only when there isn't.
  • Never stretch, recolour, outline, add a shadow to or crop a sponsor's logo to make it fit. Change its scale instead.

Do / Don't

  • Do give every logo alt text (the company name).
  • Do keep one signature sponsor where you can; two is the most the tier holds.
  • Don't mix logos in different colour treatments (full colour next to one-colour) within a tier.

Notes

  • The Partner Pavilion design shows a blue "mROC" badge beside some sponsors. It isn't built yet; use the hover card's badge for partner status until it is.
  • Hover cards: give a logo a card ({ title, body, badge, link }) and it becomes a button that opens a logo HoverCard with the logo, an optional partner badge, the name, a short text and one link. On hover with a mouse; on click, tap or Enter otherwise.
  • The logos in the preview are placeholders.

Page modules

Events

EventCalendar

Page module

Events calendar: search and filters over a month grid, a list or cards. Switch views.

Usage notes

The events calendar from the Figma Calendar page: a search and filter bar over one of three views of the same events — a month grid, a day-by-day list or a grid of cards.

Provide: events and, optionally, defaultView, defaultMonth and a promo card for the grid.

Each event: { id, title, type, format, start, end, time, href, image, flag, speakers, action }.

  • type is qualys, industry, webinar, speaking or training.
  • start and end are dates as YYYY-MM-DD; leave end out for a one-day event.
  • time is the text to show, such as "10a – 11a PST".
View Figma name What it shows
month (default) Month View A month grid with a coloured bar for each event
list List View The month's events grouped by day, each with a button
grid Grid View Every event as a card, newest first, with "Load More"

Shared parts:

  • Toolbar, on surface-neutral-100, 36px above and below (spacing-3xl): a line SearchBar (432px) on the left; on the right a FilterBar with "Event Type" and "Format" and "Reset Filters". Search and filters apply to all three views.
  • Body, on surface-neutral-300, 36px above and below, on the 1140px column.
  • Heading row: the month in h2 (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 38px), then the previous / next buttons (48 × 50px, joined, white, radius-rg). On the right, "View" and the three-button toggle (list, month, grid); the chosen one is qualys-blue with a white icon.
  • The grid view has no month; its heading is "Browse Events".

Month view:

  • "Current Month" (white, 50px tall, IBM Plex Sans SemiBold 16px) sits after the arrows and returns to today's month.
  • Legend, 36px under the heading and in line with it: a 16px radius-xs swatch and the type name, SemiBold 16px. It has the same place and spacing as the list view's legend (a 30px row, 24px between types, the swatch in the 24px slot an icon takes), so the names don't move when the view changes.
  • Calendar card, 36px below: white, radius-lg, 16px padding, shadow-drawer. Weekday names SemiBold 16px; seven columns divided by 1px stroke-neutral-400 lines; each week at least 180px tall.
  • Day: the date in IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px text-secondary. Today is misty-blue; days from the months either side are surface-neutral-200.
  • Event bar: radius-xs, 6px padding, white 14px text, 10px in from the column edges. A one-day event shows the type, the format and the title (Medium). An event of several days is one bar across its days: "Type | Format" over the title, 48px tall.
  • Compact bar: 24px tall, the title only. Used when a day has more than one event.
  • Colours: Qualys Event qualys-red, Industry Event charcoal, Webinar qualys-blue, Speaking Engagement event-speaking, Training asphalt.
  • Hover or focus on a bar shows the event's card (364px wide) beside it. Pressing the bar opens the event.

List view:

  • Legend uses the EventType icons, in the same position and with the same spacing as the month view's.
  • Day heading: "Tuesday Jan 14", IBM Plex Sans Medium 16px, 20px in from the left. 8px below it, a white card (radius-lg, 24px padding) with one row per event; rows are divided by a stroke-neutral-400 line.
  • Row: the time (150px, Medium 16px text-secondary; "All day" when an event has none), the event type icon, the title (Wix Madefor Text SemiBold 18px, two lines at most) and a secondary Button, 140px wide.
  • Button: "Register" by default. Set action on an event to change it, such as { label: 'Join Waitlist', variant: 'secondary-alt' }, or action: false to leave it out.
  • A row never shows a date, because it already sits under its day. An event of several days repeats under each of its days.

Grid view:

  • Three cards across, 24px apart, 36px between rows; each at least 440px tall. Events use EventCard, or WebinarCard when they have speakers.
  • promo (InlinePromoCard props) places a dark promo card as the sixth tile.
  • "Load More" (secondary Button), centred 36px under the grid, adds another page. pageSize sets how many tiles a page has (9).
  • Hover: the same as every card: the blue bar slides in and the outlink arrow nudges.

Responsive:

  • Tablet: the search takes its own row above the filters; weekday names shorten to "Sun"; every bar is compact; the grid has two columns.
  • Mobile: the filters become one "Filter" dropdown that opens the FilterDrawer. The month is centred between the two arrows (28px) and the toggle spans the width below it.
  • Mobile month: the calendar runs edge to edge with weekday initials, 12px dates and 20px bars showing the start of the title; "Current Month" and the legend move below it. Tapping a bar shows its card; tapping the card opens the event.
  • Mobile list: each row stacks: time, type icon and name, title, then a full-width button. The legend is hidden.
  • Mobile grid: one column.

Usage, from the Figma notes:

  • Keep event bars under the date. If a date has several events, use the compact bar with just the name.
  • The list keeps the current content structure and carries the card styles through.

Do / Don't:

  • Do keep titles short; a bar shows one line and a list row two.
  • Do give every event a type; colour alone never tells types apart, so the type is also in each bar's label and card.
  • Don't put more than about four events on one day in the month view; point people to the list instead.

Accessibility:

  • Each bar is a link whose name gives the title, type, format, dates and time. The hover card repeats this and is hidden from screen readers.
  • The view buttons are labelled "List view", "Month view" and "Grid view" and report which is pressed. The month heading announces itself when the month changes. Esc closes the card.
  • White text on qualys-blue (3.78:1) and qualys-red (4.18:1) is under 4.5:1 at 14px; kept as designed.

Notes:

  • Figma's examples mix full and compact bars on days with two events; this follows the written rule (compact="auto"). Set compact={false} to always show full bars or compact to always show compact ones.
  • Day lines are drawn in #D9DCE0; they use stroke-neutral-400. List cards are drawn with a 2% shadow; they use shadow-card. The hover card uses shadow-modal so it stands out on the white calendar.
  • The calendar file draws "Upcoming" flags in red and a blue "Multi-Day" flag, and colours each card's event type. Cards here stay as the Cards page defines them: flags in the tier colours and the type in text-accent-primary.
  • Figma's mobile bars use 8px text; this uses 10px.
  • Figma puts the mobile view toggle in the toolbar on the list and grid and under the month on the month view; here it is always under the heading.
  • The search placeholder is "Search Resources" in Figma; here it is "Search Events" (labels.search).
  • The Figma month frame shows the list button as selected; the toggle here follows the view in use.
  • Figma's note asks for grid cards to grow 5% on hover. That was dropped so every card behaves the same.

Page modules

Tables

DetailComparison

Page module

Written comparison of Qualys with up to three competitors; on mobile, one at a time. Sample data.

Usage notes

A written comparison: Qualys beside up to three competitors the reader picks, one short text per vendor for each topic. Use it when yes or no is not enough and each difference needs a sentence. For a simple feature checklist use FeatureMatrix.

Provide: columns (the first is Qualys), sections and optionally title, subtitle.

  • Columns: [{ id, name, logo, subtitle }]. Without a logo a dashed slot holds the name (competitor logos in the preview are placeholders).
  • Sections: [{ title, open, heading, copy }]. copy is keyed by column id: a string, or { heading, body } to give that vendor its own cell heading. Each section is a Drawer.
  • Picking competitors: filter chips ("Compare Qualys With · Choose up to 3"). At least one stays picked; at three, the rest are disabled until one is released. max changes the limit, defaultPicked sets the starting ids (the first two by default), picked with onChange controls it.
  • Layout: Qualys and the picked vendors share the width in equal columns, so two competitors give three columns and three give four. The Qualys cell sits on Ecru (surface-neutral-300, radius-md); the others are plain. 20px padding in every cell.
  • Type: module heading h3; cell heading title-sm (16px SemiBold); copy paragraph-rg. Keep copy to about 250 characters so columns stay a similar height; longer copy wraps and the row grows.
  • Size: a white card (radius-lg, shadow-card) in the 1140px content column. Below 240px per column the table scrolls sideways inside the card.
  • Heading and chips: above the card, on the page ground, 24px (spacing-xl) over it: the heading on the left, the chips on the right, both lined up with the card's outer edges. On a narrow screen the chips wrap under the heading. The card holds only the table, starting with the vendor logos 24px from its top.
  • Mobile (the table narrower than 768px): no card, white ground. Tabs pick one competitor; in each section the Qualys text (Ecru card) sits above the competitor's (outlined card), each under its logo.
  • Cursor: pointer on section headings, chips and tabs.
  • Accessibility: section headings are buttons (aria-expanded); each cell names its vendor for screen readers; chips are toggle buttons in a labelled group.
  • Content: describe competitors fairly and keep claims current and checked. The copy in the preview is placeholder text.
  • From the Claude Design file "Comparison Table" (Detail Comparison, desktop and mobile).

FeatureMatrix

Page module

Yes/no feature comparison with Qualys highlighted; on mobile, one competitor at a time. Sample data.

Usage notes

A yes/no comparison table: Qualys in the first, highlighted column, competitors beside it, and features grouped into topics that open and close. Use it when the claim is "we cover this, they don't" across many features. When each cell needs a sentence, use DetailComparison; for a short list of statements, MarketingTable.

Provide: columns (the first is Qualys), sections and optionally title, subtitle, noMark.

  • Columns: [{ id, name, logo, subtitle }]. Give every column its logo; without one a dashed slot holds the name (as in the preview, where competitor logos are placeholders). Two to five competitors read well on desktop.
  • Sections: [{ title, open, rows }]. Each is a Drawer; set open on the ones that start open. A row is [label, 1, 0, 1, …] or { label, values }, one value per column.
  • Marks: yes is a white tick on success, 24px circle. No is a cross on chip-bg in text-secondary (noMark="muted", the default) or white on crimson (noMark="red"). Colour is never the only signal: the tick and cross differ, and each mark is read as "Wiz: No".
  • Totals: the last row of each section counts the yes marks ("6 of 8") under the label "Supported". totalLabel renames it, formatTotal(n, total) reformats it, totals={false} removes it.
  • Highlight: an Ecru band (surface-neutral-300, radius-md) runs behind the first column from header to last row.
  • Size: a white card (radius-lg, shadow-card, 32px padding) in the 1140px content column. The label column is 2.2 parts and every vendor column one part. Rows are at least 53px tall and grow with a wrapping label; the heading is h3.
  • Overflow: the table keeps a minimum width (280px plus 128px per column) and scrolls sideways inside the card rather than squeezing. Labels wrap; vendor names in a logo slot end in an ellipsis.
  • Hover: a row takes a 3% Charcoal tint. Cursor: pointer on a section heading, default elsewhere.
  • Mobile (the table narrower than 768px): no card, white ground, 20px side padding. Qualys is compared with one competitor at a time, picked with Tabs ("Compare Qualys With"); the "Show Differences Only" Toggle hides the rows where both agree, and a section with none says "No differences in this section." Columns are 96px each.
  • Accessibility: each section's rows are a table for screen readers, labels are row headers, marks carry the vendor name. Section headings are buttons (aria-expanded).
  • Content: comparison claims must be current and checked before they go live. The data in the preview is sample data.
  • From the Claude Design file "Comparison Table" (Feature Matrix, desktop and mobile).

MarketingTable

Page module

A branded table: photo header, Feature Icon row headings, one featured column. Charcoal, tablet, mobile.

Usage notes

A branded comparison table as a page section: a Qualys Blue header row with a photo, row headings with Feature Icons, and one featured column for the Qualys point of view. It reworks the Figma component "Marketing Table With Image in Header Row".

Provide: columns and rows. The first column heads the rows; each further column takes a title or a logo (the reversed Qualys logo), a one-word subtitle, and featured on the one to draw attention to. Each row takes a title, an optional icon (a Feature Icons URL or a node) and cells: one for each column after the first, in column order. Optional: image (the header photo, as a URL or { src, size, focus }), tone (blue, the default, or dark) and label (the table's accessible name).

Use it to set a standard, a directive or a list of requirements beside what Qualys offers, a row at a time. The sample maps the CISA BOD 26-04 requirements to Qualys advantages and ROC capabilities.

  • Section on surface-neutral-200, 48px top and bottom, content in the 1140px column.
  • Card: White, radius-lg, shadow-card. The header row and the columns run to its edges.
  • Columns: the row headings take 1.25 parts and every other column 1 part. Drawn with two columns after the row headings.
  • Header row: 140px tall, with 32px padding and the copy at the bottom; 1px white rules at 30% divide the columns. The ground is qualys-blue across the top, easing to blue-gradient-end at the foot, or Charcoal (tone="dark"). The heading is h2 (SemiBold 38px, line height 1.1, −2%), 8px above the subtitle in paragraph-rg Medium; both text-inverted. A column with a logo shows it in place of the heading: the reversed Qualys logo, 37px tall.
  • Header photo: sits in the middle of the row at 72% of its width, drawn in greys and blended into the header colour, with both ends fading out. On blue it is multiplied in at 50%, so it can only darken the ground under the white copy; on Charcoal it is screened in at 16%. size changes the width and focus says how far down the photo the row is centred (header-capitol.jpg in the Images group, with focus: '54%'). Without a photo the header is the plain ground.
  • Rows: 104px tall or more, with 1px stroke-neutral-400 rules between them. Cells have 24px × 32px padding and centre their content vertically.
  • Row heading: an optional Feature Icon at 56px, 16px before the heading in h4 (SemiBold 20px, line height 1.3, −1%), text-primary, Title Case.
  • Cells: paragraph-rg (16px) in text-secondary.
  • Featured column: a surface-neutral-300 ground from under the header to the foot of the card. Its cells are Medium in text-primary, behind a 16px check icon in icon-feature, 10px before the text.
  • Tablet (768–1023px): still a table, with 20px padding, a 120px header, 48px icons, 18px row headings and a 30px logo. Column headings scale down with the section's width, to 24px at the least.
  • Mobile (under 768px): the columns stack. The header shows the first column's heading only, over the whole photo. Each row is its heading (40px icon, 18px) followed by one block per column, labelled with that column's name in the eyebrow-xs style ("QUALYS ADVANTAGES"). The featured block keeps its surface-neutral-300 ground, with radius-md and 12px padding.
  • Built as an ARIA table (role="table" with column and row headers), so each cell is announced with its headings; give it a label. The photo, icons and checks are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
  • Contrast: white on flat qualys-blue is 3.78:1, enough for the headings (24px or larger) and too little for the 16px subtitles. That is why the ground deepens toward the foot: the subtitles have 4.5:1 or more at every width (4.6:1 on desktop), and the headings 3.8:1 or more. On Charcoal both are 9:1 or more. text-secondary on surface-neutral-300 is 6.7:1. The blue check is 3.5:1 on that ground, enough for an icon; the cell's words carry the meaning.

Content:

  • Column headings: one to three words, about 14 characters at most; subtitles one word.
  • Row headings: Title Case, about 30 characters, two lines at most.
  • Cells: one phrase, about 70 characters (three lines) at most, with no full stop.
  • Four to eight rows.

Do / Don't:

  • Do feature one column, the Qualys one, and place it beside the row headings.
  • Do give every row a Feature Icon or none.
  • Do pick a photo with one clear subject in its middle (a building, a skyline) and set focus on it.
  • Don't feature the first column, or more than one column.
  • Don't flatten the blue ground to plain qualys-blue: the subtitles would drop to 3.78:1.

Where this differs from the Figma component (its desktop frame):

  • The blue deepens from top to foot, under the subtitles. In Figma it deepens from left to right, which leaves the first column's subtitle on plain Qualys Blue.
  • Rows carry Feature Icons; the Figma rows have none.
  • The Qualys column sits in the middle and is the highlighted one. In Figma it comes last and the ROC column is highlighted.
  • Featured cells are Medium in text-primary behind a check; in Figma both columns are plain grey text.
  • Row headings are Title Case throughout; the Figma sample mixes Title Case and sentence case.
  • The tablet and mobile layouts are not from Figma: this was built from the desktop frame alone, and they are new here.

Library

All

74 parts in two groups. Components are the pieces a page uses, from a single button or field to a whole form or filter bar. Page modules are the full-width sections a page is built from (a hero, a footer). Each card says whether it is a component or a pattern made of several.
